title.zh: 卷一百九十五 列傳第八十二: 忠義三
title.en: Volume 195 Biographies 82: Loyal and Righteous Acts 3
title.raw: 卷一百九十五 列傳第八十二: 忠義三 Volume 195 Biographies 82: Loyal and Righteous Acts 3

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤，字蒼崖，​​畏吾兒氏，駙馬都尉、中書丞相、封高昌王雪雪的斤之孫，駙馬都尉、江浙行省丞相、封荊南王朵爾的斤之子也。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin, style name Cangya, of the Uyghur clan, was the grandson of the imperial son-in-law commissioner, Central Secretariat chancellor, and enfeoffed Prince of Gaochang Xuexue's jin, and the son of the imperial son-in-law commissioner, Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat chancellor, and enfeoffed Prince of Jingnan Duo'erde's jin.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin, whose style name was Cangya, belonged to the Uyghur clan. He was the grandson of Xuexue's jin—imperial son-in-law commissioner, chancellor of the Central Secretariat, and Prince of Gaochang—and the son of Duo'erde's jin—imperial son-in-law commissioner, chancellor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Prince of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 倜儻好學，曉音律。

translations.literal: He was free-spirited and fond of learning, and understood music.
translations.idiomatic: Unconventional and studious, he was also versed in music.

sentences.zh: 初用父廕，同知信州路事，又移建德路。

translations.literal: At first he entered office through his father's privilege, as associate administrator of Xinzhou Circuit, and was later transferred to Jiande Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service through his father's hereditary privilege as associate administrator of Xinzhou Circuit, then was reassigned to Jiande Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會徽寇犯遂安，伯顏不花的斤將義兵平之，又擒淳安叛賊方清之，以功升本路總管。

translations.literal: When Huizhou bandits invaded Suian, Bayan Buhua's jin led righteous troops to pacify them, and also captured the Chun'an rebel Fang Qingzhi; for these merits he was promoted to circuit intendant of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Huizhou raided Suian, he led local militia to suppress them and captured the Chun'an rebel Fang Qingzhi. For these achievements he was promoted to intendant of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 至正十六年，授衢州路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhizheng, he was appointed darughachi of Quzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356 he was appointed darughachi of Quzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，行樞密院判官阿魯灰引兵經衢州，軍無紀律，所過輒大剽掠。

translations.literal: The next year, the acting Privy Council vice commissioner Aruhui led troops through Quzhou; the army had no discipline and wherever it passed it plundered on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, Acting Privy Council vice commissioner Aruhui marched through Quzhou with troops that lacked all discipline and looted heavily wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤曰：「阿魯灰以官軍而為民患，此國賊也，可縱之乎！」

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin said: "Aruhui uses government troops to become a scourge upon the people—this is a traitor to the state; can he be allowed to go free!"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin said, "Aruhui turns imperial troops into a plague upon the people. He is a traitor to the realm. How can we let him pass?"

sentences.zh: 乃帥兵逐之出境，郡賴以寧。

translations.literal: He then led troops to drive him beyond the border, and the prefecture relied on this to be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops to drive Aruhui out of the jurisdiction, and the prefecture was spared further harm.

sentences.zh: 升浙東都元帥，守禦衢州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to commander-in-chief of Eastern Zhejiang and defended Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander-in-chief of Eastern Zhejiang and charged with the defense of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢江東道廉訪副使，階中大夫。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was elevated to vice censor of the Jiangdong Circuit, with the rank of junior grand master.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangdong surveillance commission, with the civil rank of junior grand master.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，江西陳友諒遣賊黨王奉國等，號二十萬，寇信州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighteenth year, Chen Youliang of Jiangxi sent the bandit leader Wang Fengguo and others, claiming two hundred thousand men, to invade Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1358, Chen Youliang of Jiangxi sent Wang Fengguo and other rebel commanders—claiming an army of two hundred thousand—to attack Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，伯顏不花的斤自衢引兵援焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, Bayan Buhua's jin led troops from Qu to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The following January he marched from Quzhou with a relief force.

sentences.zh: 及至，遇奉國城東，力戰，破走之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he encountered Fengguo east of the city, fought fiercely, and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he met Fengguo east of the city, fought hard, and drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 時鎮南王子大聖奴、樞密院判官席閏等屯兵城中，聞伯顏不花的斤至，爭開門出迎，羅拜馬前。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Zhennan's son Dashengnu, Privy Council vice commissioner Xi Run, and others were encamped in the city; hearing that Bayan Buhua's jin had come, they vied to open the gates and go out to welcome him, bowing in rows before his horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhennan's son Dashengnu, Privy Council vice commissioner Xi Run, and other defenders were then garrisoned inside the city. When they heard Bayan Buhua's jin had arrived, they rushed to open the gates and welcome him, prostrating themselves in rows before his horse.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤登城四顧，誓以破賊自許。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin ascended the wall and looked about on all sides, vowing to break the bandits as his pledge to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin climbed the wall, surveyed the scene on every side, and vowed that he would destroy the rebels.

sentences.zh: 後數日，賊復來攻城，伯顏不花的斤大饗士卒，約曰：「今日破賊，不用命者斬！」

translations.literal: Several days later the bandits again came to attack the city; Bayan Buhua's jin held a great feast for the soldiers and stipulated: "Today we break the bandits—whoever does not obey orders shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the rebels returned to besiege the city. Bayan Buhua's jin held a great feast for the troops and declared, "Whoever fails to obey orders today shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 乃命大都閭將阿速諸軍及民義為左翼，出南門；

translations.literal: He then ordered the grand commander to lead the Asud troops and civilian volunteers as the left wing, out through the south gate;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the grand commander to take the Asud troops and civilian volunteers as the left wing through the south gate;

sentences.zh: 高義、範則忠將信陽一軍為右翼，出北門；

translations.literal: Gao Yi and Fan Zezhong to lead the Xinyang army as the right wing, out through the north gate;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yi and Fan Zezhong to lead the Xinyang garrison as the right wing through the north gate;

sentences.zh: 自與忽都不花將沿海諸軍為中軍，出西門。

translations.literal: he himself with Hudubuhua to lead the coastal armies as the center army, out through the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: and he himself, with Hudubuhua, to lead the coastal forces as the center through the west gate.

sentences.zh: 部伍既整，因奮擊入賊營，斬首數千級，賊亂，幾擒奉國。

translations.literal: Once the ranks were arrayed, they therefore struck fiercely into the bandit camp, beheading several thousand; the bandits were thrown into disorder, and Fengguo was nearly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the formations were set, they charged into the rebel camp, killing several thousand men. The enemy ranks broke, and Fengguo was nearly taken.

sentences.zh: 適賊將突至，我軍入其營者咸沒，其勢將殆，忽都不花复勒兵力戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Just then bandit generals arrived in a sudden rush; those of our army who had entered their camp were all lost, and the situation was about to collapse, but Hudubuhua again drove the troops and fought fiercely, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Just then rebel reinforcements surged in. Every man of ours who had penetrated the camp was cut off, and defeat seemed imminent—until Hudubuhua rallied the troops and fought on until the enemy was routed.

sentences.zh: 二月，友諒弟友德營於城東，繞城植木柵，攻我益急。

translations.literal: In the second month, Youliang's younger brother Youde encamped east of the city, planted wooden palisades around the wall, and attacked us with increasing urgency.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Youliang's younger brother Youde encamped east of the city, ringed it with wooden palisades, and pressed the assault ever harder.

sentences.zh: 又遣偽萬戶周伯嘉來說降，高義潛與之通，紿忽都不花等，謂與奉國相見則兵釁可解。

translations.literal: He also sent the false ten-thousand-household commander Zhou Bojia to urge surrender; Gao Yi secretly communicated with him and deceived Hudubuhua and others, saying that if they met Fengguo the military conflict could be resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also sent the bogus commander Zhou Bojia to negotiate surrender. Gao Yi secretly colluded with him and tricked Hudubuhua and the others into believing that a meeting with Fengguo would end the fighting.

sentences.zh: 忽都不花信之，率則忠等十人往見，奉國囚之不遣。

translations.literal: Hudubuhua believed this, and led Zezhong and nine others to go see him; Fengguo imprisoned them and would not release them.
translations.idiomatic: Hudubuhua believed him and went with Zezhong and nine other officers to the meeting. Fengguo seized them and refused to let them return.

sentences.zh: 明日，奉國令高義以計來誘伯顏不花的斤，時伯顏不花的斤坐城上，見高義單騎來，伯顏不花的斤謂曰：「汝誘十帥，無一人還，今復來誘我耶？

translations.literal: The next day Fengguo ordered Gao Yi by stratagem to lure Bayan Buhua's jin; at that time Bayan Buhua's jin was seated on the wall and saw Gao Yi come alone on horseback. Bayan Buhua's jin said to him: "You lured away ten commanders and not one returned—do you come now again to lure me?
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fengguo sent Gao Yi to lure Bayan Buhua's jin by another ruse. Bayan Buhua's jin was on the wall when he saw Gao Yi ride up alone. He said, "You lured away ten commanders and not one came back. Do you think you can lure me now?

sentences.zh: 我頭可斷，足不可移！」

translations.literal: My head may be cut off, but my feet will not move!"
translations.idiomatic: My head may be cut off, but my feet will not budge!"

sentences.zh: 乃數其罪，斬之。

translations.literal: He then enumerated his crimes and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Gao Yi's crimes and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 由是日夜與賊鏖戰，糧竭矢盡，而氣不少衰。

translations.literal: From this he fought the bandits day and night in bitter combat; grain was exhausted and arrows spent, yet his spirit did not decline in the least.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he fought the rebels day and night. Provisions ran out and arrows were spent, yet the defenders' morale did not falter.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，有大呼於城下者，曰：「有詔。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, someone shouted loudly below the wall, saying: "There is an edict."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer someone shouted from below the wall, "An edict has arrived!"

sentences.zh: 參謀海魯丁臨城問之曰：「何來？」

translations.literal: The staff officer Hairuding came to the wall and asked him: "From where?"
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Hairuding called down from the wall, "From where?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「江西來。」

translations.literal: He said: "From Jiangxi."
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, "From Jiangxi."

sentences.zh: 海魯丁曰：「如此，乃賊耳。

translations.literal: Hairuding said: "If so, then you are bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hairuding said, "Then you are rebels.

sentences.zh: 吾元朝臣子，可受爾偽詔乎？」

translations.literal: We are subjects of the Yuan court—can we receive your false edict?"
translations.idiomatic: We are subjects of the Yuan dynasty. Do you think we would accept your counterfeit edict?"

sentences.zh: 呼者曰：「我主聞信州久不下，知爾忠義，故來詔。

translations.literal: The shouter said: "My lord heard that Xinzhou long would not fall and knew your loyalty and righteousness, therefore he came with an edict.
translations.idiomatic: The caller replied, "My lord heard that Xinzhou has held out so long. Knowing your loyalty, he has sent this message.

sentences.zh: 爾徒守空城，欲何為耶？」

translations.literal: You vainly defend an empty city—what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you cling to an empty city for nothing?"

sentences.zh: 海魯丁曰：「汝聞張睢陽事乎？」

translations.literal: Hairuding said: "Have you heard of Zhang Xunyang's affair?"
translations.idiomatic: Hairuding asked, "Have you heard what Zhang Xunyang did at Suiyang?"

sentences.zh: 偽使者不答而去。

translations.literal: The false envoy made no reply and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The false envoy offered no answer and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤笑曰：「賊欲我降爾。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin laughed and said: "The bandits want us to surrender, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin laughed and said, "The rebels only want us to surrender.

sentences.zh: 城存與存，城亡與亡，吾計之熟矣。」

translations.literal: If the city survives, I survive; if the city perishes, I perish—I have considered this thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: If the city stands, I stand; if the city falls, I fall. My mind is made up."

sentences.zh: 時軍民唯食草苗茶紙，既盡，括靴底煮食之，又盡，掘鼠羅雀，及殺老弱以食。

translations.literal: At that time soldiers and civilians had only grass sprouts, tea, and paper to eat; when these were gone, they scraped boot soles and boiled them to eat; when these too were gone, they dug out rats and netted sparrows, and even killed the old and weak for food.
translations.idiomatic: By then soldiers and civilians had eaten only grass sprouts, tea leaves, and paper. When those were gone they boiled boot leather; when that was gone they hunted rats and snared sparrows, and finally killed the old and weak for food.

sentences.zh: 五月，大破賊兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they inflicted a great defeat on the bandit troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they won a major victory over the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 六月，奉國親來攻城，晝夜不息者逾旬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Fengguo came in person to attack the city, attacking day and night without cease for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Fengguo came in person to assault the city, attacking day and night without pause for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 賊皆穴地百餘所，或魚貫梯城而上。

translations.literal: The bandits all tunneled the ground in more than a hundred places, or climbed the wall in single file on ladders.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dug more than a hundred tunnels and sent men up scaling ladders in single file.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤登城，麾兵拒之。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin ascended the wall and directed the troops to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin took the wall and directed the defense.

sentences.zh: 已而士卒力疲，不能戰，萬戶顧馬兒以城叛，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Before long the soldiers' strength was exhausted and they could not fight; the ten-thousand-household commander Gu Ma'er surrendered the city in treason, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the troops were exhausted and could fight no more. The commander Gu Ma'er betrayed the city, and it fell.

sentences.zh: 席閏出降，大聖奴、海魯丁皆死之，伯顏不花的斤力戰不勝，遂自刎。

translations.literal: Xi Run came out and surrendered; Dashengnu and Hairuding all died; Bayan Buhua's jin fought fiercely but could not prevail, and thereupon cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Run surrendered. Dashengnu and Hairuding were killed. Bayan Buhua's jin fought on until defeat was certain, then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 其部將蔡誠，盡殺妻子，及蔣廣奮力巷戰。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Cai Cheng killed his wife and children entirely, and together with Jiang Guang fought fiercely in the alleys.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Cai Cheng killed his wife and children, then fought alongside Jiang Guang in the streets.

sentences.zh: 誠遇害死，廣為奉國所執，愛廣勇敢，使之降，廣曰：「我寧為忠死，不為降生。

translations.literal: Cheng met with disaster and died; Guang was seized by Fengguo, who admired Guang's bravery and urged him to surrender. Guang said: "I would rather die in loyalty than live in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was killed in the fighting. Guang was captured by Fengguo, who admired his courage and urged him to submit. Guang said, "I would rather die loyal than live a traitor.

sentences.zh: 汝等草中一盜爾，吾豈屈汝乎！」

translations.literal: You are but a bandit in the grass—how could I bow to you!"
translations.idiomatic: You are nothing but bandits in the weeds. Why should I bow to you?"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，磔廣於竿，廣大罵而絕。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and dismembered Guang on a pole; Guang cursed loudly until he expired.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in their fury dismembered him on a stake. Guang cursed them until his last breath.

sentences.zh: 有陳受者，信小民也。

translations.literal: There was one Chen Shou, a petty commoner of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Chen Shou, a commoner of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤知受有膂力，募為義兵。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin knew that Shou had physical strength and recruited him as a righteous soldier.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin, knowing Chen Shou's strength, enrolled him in the militia.

sentences.zh: 尋戰敗，為賊擒，痛罵不屈，賊焚殺之。

translations.literal: Soon he was defeated in battle, seized by bandits, and though he cursed them bitterly would not yield; the bandits burned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon captured in defeat. He cursed the rebels without yielding, and they burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 先是，伯顏不花的斤之援信州也，嘗南望泣下，曰：「我為天子司憲，視彼城之危急，忍坐視乎！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bayan Buhua's jin went to relieve Xinzhou, he once looked southward and wept, saying: "I am the Son of Heaven's overseer of law—seeing that city's peril, how could I sit and watch!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Bayan Buhua's jin set out to relieve Xinzhou, he once looked southward and wept. He said, "I serve the Son of Heaven as censor. How can I sit idle while that city faces ruin?

sentences.zh: 吾知上報天子，下拯生民，餘皆無可卹。

translations.literal: I know only to repay the Son of Heaven above and rescue the living people below—all else is not worth grieving over.
translations.idiomatic: I know only to answer to the throne above and save the people below. Nothing else concerns me.

sentences.zh: 所念者，太夫人耳。」

translations.literal: What I think of is only the Lady Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: Only my mother weighs on my mind."

sentences.zh: 即日入拜其母鮮于氏曰：「兒今不得事母矣。」

translations.literal: That same day he went in to bow to his mother, Lady Xianyu, and said: "Your son today can no longer serve his mother."
translations.idiomatic: That same day he went to his mother, Lady Xianyu, and said, "Mother, I can no longer attend you."

sentences.zh: 母曰：「爾為忠臣，吾即死，復何憾！」

translations.literal: His mother said: "You are a loyal minister—if I die at once, what regret remains!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother replied, "If you die a loyal minister, what regret could I have in dying myself?"

sentences.zh: 鮮于氏，太常典簿樞之女也。

translations.literal: Lady Xianyu was the daughter of the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xianyu was the daughter of Shu, director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 伯顏不花的斤因命子也先不花，奉其母間道入福建，以江東廉訪司印送行御史臺，遂力守孤城而死。

translations.literal: Bayan Buhua's jin therefore ordered his son Yexian Buhua to escort his mother by a secret route into Fujian, and sent the Jiangdong surveillance commission seal to the traveling censorate; he then strove to defend the isolated city and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan Buhua's jin then sent his son Yexian Buhua to escort his mother by a hidden route into Fujian and forwarded the Jiangdong surveillance seal to the traveling censorate. He himself held the isolated city to the death.

sentences.zh: 朝廷賜諡曰桓敏。

translations.literal: The court bestowed the posthumous title Huamin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the posthumous title Huamin.

sentences.zh: 樊執敬，字時中，濟寧鄆城人。

translations.literal: Fan Zhijing, style name Shizhong, was a man of Yuncheng in Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhijing, whose style name was Shizhong, came from Yuncheng in Jining.

sentences.zh: 性警敏好學，由國子生擢授經郎。

translations.literal: By nature alert and quick-witted, fond of learning, he was selected from the Imperial Academy students and appointed classics clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and studious, he was selected from the Imperial Academy and appointed classics clerk.

sentences.zh: 嘗見帝師不拜，或諗之曰：「帝師，天子素崇重，王公大臣見必俯伏作禮，公獨不拜，何也？」

translations.literal: Once when he saw the Imperial Preceptor he did not bow; someone questioned him, saying: "The Imperial Preceptor is what the Son of Heaven has always honored and esteemed—when princes and great ministers see him they must prostrate themselves in ceremony. You alone do not bow—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he met the Imperial Preceptor, he did not bow. Someone asked him, "The Son of Heaven holds the Imperial Preceptor in the highest esteem. Princes and ministers prostrate themselves before him. Why do you alone refuse to bow?"

sentences.zh: 執敬曰：「吾孔氏之徒，知尊孔氏而已，何拜異教為？」

translations.literal: Zhijing said: "I am a follower of Master Kong—I know only to honor Master Kong; why bow to an alien teaching?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing replied, "I am a follower of Confucius. I honor only Confucius. Why should I bow to a foreign faith?"

sentences.zh: 歷官至侍御史。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 至正七年，擢山南道廉訪使，俄移湖北道。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhizheng he was elevated to surveillance commissioner of the Shannan Circuit, and shortly was transferred to the Hubei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1347 he was appointed surveillance commissioner of the Shannan Circuit and soon transferred to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十年，授江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1350 he was made associate administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，督海運於平江，卜日將發，官大宴犒於海口。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year he supervised sea transport at Pingjiang; an auspicious day for departure was chosen, and officials held a great feast to reward the troops at the harbor mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1352 he supervised the sea transport at Pingjiang. With the sailing date set, officials held a great feast for the crews at the harbor.

sentences.zh: 俄有客船自外至，驗其券信令入，而不虞其為海寇也。

translations.literal: Shortly a guest ship came from outside; they verified its passes and trusted them, allowing it to enter, yet did not anticipate that it was sea pirates.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a merchant vessel arrived from outside. Its papers were checked and found in order, so it was admitted—no one suspected it was a pirate ship.

sentences.zh: 既入港，即縱火鼓譟。

translations.literal: Once it had entered the harbor, they immediately set fires and beat drums in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the harbor, the crew set fires and raised a clamor of drums.

sentences.zh: 時變起倉猝，軍民擾亂，賊竟焚舟劫糧以去。

translations.literal: The disturbance arose in sudden haste; soldiers and civilians were thrown into turmoil, and the bandits ultimately burned the ships and plundered the grain before departing.
translations.idiomatic: The attack came without warning. Troops and civilians fell into chaos, and the pirates burned the ships, seized the grain, and fled.

sentences.zh: 執敬既走入崑山，自咎於失防，心鬱鬱不解。

translations.literal: Zhijing had already fled into Kunshan and blamed himself for the failure of defense; his heart was depressed and would not ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had fled to Kunshan. He blamed himself for the lapse in defense and could not shake his grief.

sentences.zh: 及還省，而昱嶺關有警，平章政事月魯帖木兒引軍拒之，賊不得進。

translations.literal: When he returned to the secretariat, there was an alarm at Yuling Pass; the grand councillor Yelü Temür led troops to resist, and the bandits could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the secretariat, rebels threatened Yuling Pass. Grand councillor Yelü Temür led troops to block them, and the enemy could not break through.

sentences.zh: 月魯帖木兒俄以疾卒，賊遂犯餘杭。

translations.literal: Yelü Temür shortly died of illness, and the bandits thereupon invaded Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Temür soon died of illness, and the rebels then struck Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 執敬時已被命討賊海上，至是事急，不得捨去，與平章政事定定治事省中，調兵出戰，皆不利。

translations.literal: Zhijing had at that time already been ordered to pursue bandits at sea; when the matter became urgent he could not abandon his post, and together with the grand councillor Dingding he administered affairs in the secretariat and deployed troops to battle—all were unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had already been ordered to pursue pirates at sea, but the crisis left him no choice but to stay. He and grand councillor Dingding directed affairs from the secretariat and sent troops into battle, yet every engagement went badly.

sentences.zh: 掾史蘇友龍素抗直有為，進言於執敬曰：「賊且至，城內空虛無備，奈何？」

translations.literal: The clerk Su Youlong was by nature upright and forceful; he advanced words to Zhijing, saying: "The bandits are about to arrive—the city within is empty and without preparations; what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Su Youlong, known for his forthrightness and resolve, urged Zhijing, "The rebels are almost here. The city is empty and undefended. What will you do?"

sentences.zh: 執敬曰：「吾淬礪戈矛，當殲賊以報國，儻或不克，有死而已，何畏哉！」

translations.literal: Zhijing said: "I have sharpened spears and halberds—I shall destroy the bandits to repay the state. If perchance I do not prevail, there is only death; what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing answered, "I have sharpened my weapons. I will destroy the rebels for the realm. If I fail, I die—that is all. What is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 俄報賊已至，執敬遽上馬，帥眾而出。

translations.literal: Shortly word came that the bandits had already arrived; Zhijing hastily mounted his horse and led the multitude out.
translations.idiomatic: Word soon came that the rebels had arrived. Zhijing mounted at once and led his men out.

sentences.zh: 中途與賊遇，乃射死賊四人，賊又逐之，射死三人。

translations.literal: Midway they encountered the bandits; he shot and killed four bandits; the bandits again pursued him, and he shot and killed three.
translations.idiomatic: On the way he met the enemy and killed four rebels with his bow. When they pursued him, he killed three more.

sentences.zh: 已而賊來方盛，填咽街巷，且縱火，眾皆潰去。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits came in full force, filling and choking the streets and alleys, and also set fires; the multitude all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels came in overwhelming numbers, choking the streets and setting fires. His men broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊知其無援，呼執敬降，執敬怒叱之曰：「逆賊！

translations.literal: The bandits knew he had no reinforcements and called on Zhijing to surrender. Zhijing angrily shouted at them: "Rebel traitors!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he had no support, the rebels called on him to surrender. Zhijing roared back, "Traitors!

sentences.zh: 守關吏不謹，汝得至此，恨不碎汝萬段，何謂降耶！」

translations.literal: The pass guards were not careful, so you reached here—I regret only that I cannot cut you into ten thousand pieces; what talk is there of surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: The pass guards were negligent, or you would never have come this far. I only regret I cannot hack you to pieces. Who speaks of surrender?"

sentences.zh: 乃奮刀斫賊，因中槍而墮。

translations.literal: He then wielded his blade fiercely to hack the bandits, and thereby was struck by a spear and fell.
translations.idiomatic: He swung his blade at the enemy and was struck down by a spear.

sentences.zh: 從僕田也先馳救之，亦中槍死。

translations.literal: His attendant servant Tian Yexian galloped to rescue him and also was struck by a spear and died.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Tian Yexian rushed to his aid and was also killed by a spear.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈翰林學士承旨、榮祿大夫、柱國，追封魯國公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Hanlin academician ex officio, grand master of glorious blessing, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, with the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Hanlin academician ex officio, grand master of glorious blessing, and pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Lu with the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 全普庵撒里，字子仁，高昌人。

translations.literal: Quan Pu'ansali, style name Ziren, was a man of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Pu'ansali, whose style name was Ziren, came from Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 初為中書省檢校，時太師汪家奴擅權用事，臺諫無敢言者，普庵撒​​里獨於眾中歷數其過，諤諤無懼色。

translations.literal: At first he was a verifier of the Central Secretariat; at that time the Grand Preceptor Wangjianu monopolized power and handled affairs, and the censorate and remonstrance offices dared not speak—Pu'ansali alone in the assembly enumerated his faults, speaking bluntly without a trace of fear.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as verifier in the Central Secretariat. At that time Grand Preceptor Wangjianu held unchecked power, and no censor dared speak against him. Pu'ansali alone rose in assembly to list Wangjianu's crimes, speaking bluntly without fear.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，即首劾汪家奴十罪，乃見黜。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating censor, he immediately in the first memorial impeached Wangjianu for ten crimes, and was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating censor, he immediately impeached Wangjianu on ten counts and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 然而氣節益自振，不以摧衄遂阻，歷詆權貴，朝臣莫不畏栗。

translations.literal: Yet his moral spirit only stirred itself more, not deterred by setback and obstruction; he repeatedly denounced the powerful and noble, and court ministers all feared and trembled before him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his resolve only grew stronger. Undeterred by disgrace, he went on denouncing the powerful until courtiers trembled at his name.

sentences.zh: 出為廣東廉訪使，尋除兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He went out as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, and shortly was removed to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, then appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授贛州路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed darughachi of Ganzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed darughachi of Ganzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至郡，發摘奸惡，一郡肅然。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the prefecture he exposed and seized the wicked; the whole prefecture became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he exposed and punished wrongdoers until the whole prefecture was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，潁州盜起，即修築城壘，旬月之間，守御之具畢備。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng bandits arose in Yingzhou; he immediately repaired and built ramparts, and within a month and ten days defensive equipment was fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 rebels rose in Yingzhou. He at once fortified the walls, and within a month all defenses were ready.

sentences.zh: 於是發公帑，募勇士，得兵三千人，日練習之，皆可用。

translations.literal: Thereupon he disbursed public funds, recruited brave warriors, obtained three thousand troops, drilled them daily, and all were usable.
translations.idiomatic: He drew on public funds to recruit warriors, raised three thousand men, and drilled them daily until they were fit for battle.

sentences.zh: 屬邑有為賊所陷者，往往遣兵復之，境內悉安。

translations.literal: Where subordinate districts had been overrun by bandits, he often sent troops to recover them, and within his jurisdiction all was secure.
translations.idiomatic: When neighboring districts fell to rebels, he sent troops to recover them until his entire jurisdiction was secure.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以功拜江西行省參政，分省於贛。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for merit he was appointed associate administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, with a sub-secretariat at Gan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1356, for his achievements, he was made associate administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat with authority centered at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，江西下流諸郡皆為陳友諒所據，乃與總管哈海赤戮力同守。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, all the lower-stream prefectures of Jiangxi were seized by Chen Youliang; he therefore joined with the circuit intendant Hahaichi to strive together in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In 1358, Chen Youliang seized the lower Yangzi prefectures of Jiangxi. Pu'ansali and circuit intendant Hahaichi joined forces to hold Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 友諒遣其將幸文才率兵圍贛，使人脅之降。

translations.literal: Youliang sent his general Xing Wencai to lead troops and besiege Gan, and sent men to coerce them into surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang sent his general Xing Wencai to besiege Ganzhou and envoys to demand surrender.

sentences.zh: 普庵撒里斬其使，日擐甲登城拒之。

translations.literal: Pu'ansali beheaded his envoys and daily donned armor to ascend the wall and resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Pu'ansali beheaded the envoys and daily donned armor to defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 力戰凡四月，兵少食盡，義兵萬戶馬合某沙欲舉城降賊，普庵撒里不從，遂自剄。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely for four months in all; troops were few and food exhausted. The righteous-soldier commander Ma Hemousha wished to surrender the city to the bandits; Pu'ansali would not agree and thereupon cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: For four months he fought on as supplies dwindled. The militia commander Ma Hemousha tried to surrender the city to the rebels, but Pu'ansali refused and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷贈諡曰儆哀。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court bestowed the posthumous title Jing'ai.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was granted the posthumous title Jing'ai.

sentences.zh: 哈海赤守贛尤有功，城陷之日，賊將脅之使降，哈海赤謂之曰：「與汝戰者我也，爾賊毋殺贛民，當速殺我耳。」

translations.literal: Hahaichi's defense of Gan was especially meritorious. On the day the city fell, a bandit general coerced him to surrender. Hahaichi said to him: "It is I who fought you—you bandits must not kill the people of Gan; you should kill me quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Hahaichi had done the most to defend Ganzhou. When the city fell, a rebel commander tried to force him to submit. Hahaichi said, "I am the one who fought you. Do not harm the people of Ganzhou—kill me instead."

sentences.zh: 遂見殺。

translations.literal: He was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 周鏜，字以聲，瀏陽州人。

translations.literal: Zhou Tang, style name Yisheng, was a man of Liuyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tang, whose style name was Yisheng, came from Liuyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 篤學通《春秋》，登泰定四年進士第，授衡陽縣丞，再調大冶縣尹。

translations.literal: He studied earnestly and mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Taiding, was appointed assistant magistrate of Hengyang County, and was transferred again to magistrate of Daye County.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted scholar of the Spring and Autumn Annals, he passed the jinshi examination in 1327, served as assistant magistrate of Hengyang County, and was later transferred to magistrate of Daye County.

sentences.zh: 縣有豪民，持官府短長，號為難治，鏜狀若尪懦，而毅然有威不可犯，抑豪強，惠窮民，治行遂為諸縣最。

translations.literal: The county had powerful families who held the government's weaknesses and were called difficult to govern. Tang appeared frail and timid, yet was resolute with an authority that could not be violated; he suppressed the powerful and favored the poor, and his governance became the foremost among all counties.
translations.idiomatic: The county had powerful families who knew the government's weaknesses and were considered ungovernable. Tang seemed frail and timid, yet carried an authority none could defy. He suppressed the powerful, aided the poor, and his administration became the best in the region.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子助教。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會修《功臣列傳》，擢翰林國史編修官。

translations.literal: When the Meritorious Ministers Biographies was being compiled, he was elevated to Hanlin historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: While the Meritorious Ministers Biographies was being compiled, he was appointed Hanlin historiographer.

sentences.zh: 乃出為四川行省儒學提舉，便道還家。

translations.literal: He then went out as Confucian educational commissioner of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and returned home by a convenient route.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as Confucian educational commissioner of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat and took the opportunity to return home.

sentences.zh: 無何，盜起，湖南、北郡縣皆陷。

translations.literal: Before long bandits arose, and the prefectures and counties of Hunan north and south all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels rose, and prefectures throughout northern and southern Hunan fell.

sentences.zh: 瀏陽無城守，盜至，民皆驚竄。

translations.literal: Liuyang had no walls to defend; when bandits arrived the people all fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Liuyang had no city walls. When rebels arrived, the people fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 鏜告其兄弟使遠引，自謂「我受國恩，脫不幸，必死，毋為相累也」。

translations.literal: Tang told his brothers to withdraw far away, saying himself: "I have received the state's grace; if misfortune comes, I must die—do not let me drag you down."
translations.idiomatic: Tang urged his brothers to flee, saying, "I owe the state my life. If the worst comes, I must die—do not let me drag you down."

sentences.zh: 賊至，得鏜，欲推以為主，鏜唯瞠目厲聲大罵，賊知其不可屈。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived and seized Tang, they wished to make him their leader. Tang only glared with bulging eyes and cursed loudly; the bandits knew he could not be bent.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels captured him and tried to make him their leader. Tang only glared and cursed them fiercely. The rebels knew he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 乃殺之。

translations.literal: They thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him.

sentences.zh: 鏜同時有謝一魯字至道者，亦瀏陽人。

translations.literal: At the same time as Tang there was Xie Yilu, style name Zhidao, also a man of Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: A contemporary of Tang was Xie Yilu, whose style name was Zhidao, also from Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 至元乙亥鄉貢進士，嘗為石林書院山長。

translations.literal: A presented scholar of the yihai year of Zhiyuan, he once served as head of the Shilin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A presented scholar of 1275, he had served as head of the Shilin Academy.

sentences.zh: 賊陷潭州，一魯奉親匿巖谷中。

translations.literal: When bandits overran Tanzhou, Yilu escorted his parents to hide in ravines and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Tanzhou, Yilu hid his parents in the hills.

sentences.zh: 官兵复郡邑，亡者稍歸，乃還理故業。

translations.literal: When government troops recovered the prefectures and counties, those who had fled gradually returned, and he resumed his former occupation.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial troops recovered the region, refugees gradually returned, and he resumed his former work.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊復至，生縛一魯。

translations.literal: Shortly the bandits came again and bound Yilu alive.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels returned and seized Yilu alive.

sentences.zh: 一魯罵賊甚厲，舉家咸遇害。

translations.literal: Yilu cursed the bandits very fiercely, and his whole family likewise met with disaster and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them bitterly, and his entire family was killed.

sentences.zh: 聶炳，字韞夫，江夏人。

translations.literal: Nie Bing, style name Yunfu, was a man of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Bing, whose style name was Yunfu, came from Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 元統元年進士，授承事郎、同知平昌州事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Yuantong, he was appointed court gentleman and associate administrator of Pingchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1333, he was appointed court gentleman and associate administrator of Pingchang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 炳蚤孤，其母改適，自平昌還，始知之，即迎其母以歸。

translations.literal: Bing was orphaned early; his mother remarried. When he returned from Pingchang he first learned of this and at once went to welcome his mother back.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he did not learn until returning from Pingchang that his mother had remarried. He at once went to bring her home.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉寶慶路推官。

translations.literal: After a long while he was transferred to judicial officer of Baqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to judicial officer of Baqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會峒徭寇邊，湖廣行省右丞禿赤統兵討之，屯於武岡，以炳攝分省理問官。

translations.literal: When Dong-Yao bandits raided the border, the right vice censor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat Tuchi led troops to subdue them, encamped at Wugang, and appointed Bing acting sub-secretariat judicial inquirer.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong-Yao tribesmen raided the border, Huguang vice censor Tuchi led troops against them from Wugang and appointed Bing acting judicial inquirer of the sub-secretariat.

sentences.zh: 悍卒所至掠民為俘，炳言於禿赤，釋其無驗者數千人。

translations.literal: Fierce soldiers wherever they went seized civilians as captives; Bing spoke to Tuchi and released several thousand of those without evidence.
translations.idiomatic: His brutal troops seized civilians as captives wherever they went. Bing persuaded Tuchi to release several thousand who had been taken without cause.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，遷知荊門州，才半歲，淮、漢賊起，荊門不守，炳出，募土兵，得眾七萬，复荊門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng he was transferred to prefect of Jingmen Prefecture. After only half a year, Huai and Han bandits arose and Jingmen could not be held. Bing went out, recruited local troops, obtained seventy thousand men, and recovered Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 he was made prefect of Jingmen. Half a year later, rebels from the Huai and Han regions rose and Jingmen fell. Bing raised local troops—seventy thousand men—and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 又與四川行省平章政事咬住复江陵，其功居多。

translations.literal: He also together with the Sichuan Branch Secretariat grand councillor Qiaozhu recovered Jiangling, and his merit was the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Sichuan grand councillor Qiaozhu in recovering Jiangling, contributing the greater share of the victory.

sentences.zh: 既而蘄、黃、安陸之賊，其勢復振，賊將俞君正合兵來攻荊門，炳率孤軍晝夜血戰，援絕城陷，為賊所執。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits of Qi, Huang, and Anlu, their momentum reviving again, the bandit general Yu Junzheng combined forces to attack Jingmen. Bing led an isolated army fighting day and night in bloody combat; reinforcements were cut off and the city fell; he was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels from Qi, Huang, and Anlu rallied again. Rebel general Yu Junzheng besieged Jingmen. Bing led a lone force in day-and-night fighting until reinforcements failed and the city fell. He was captured.

sentences.zh: 極口罵不絕，賊以刀抉其齒盡，乃斷左臂而支解之。

translations.literal: He cursed without cease; the bandits used knives to pry out all his teeth, then severed his left arm and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them without pause. The rebels pried out his teeth, severed his left arm, and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊陷潛江縣，達魯花赤明安達爾率勇敢出擊，擒其偽將劉萬戶。

translations.literal: Before long bandits overran Qianjiang County. The darughachi Mingandár led the brave in a sortie and captured their false commander Liu Wanhu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, rebels overran Qianjiang County. Darughachi Mingandár led a sortie and captured the rebel commander Liu Wanhu.

sentences.zh: 進營蘆伏，賊眾奄至，出鬥死，其家殲焉。

translations.literal: Advancing to encamp at Lufu, bandit masses suddenly arrived; he went out to fight and died, and his family was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to camp at Lufu, but rebel forces suddenly surrounded him. He fought out and was killed, and his family perished with him.

sentences.zh: 一子桂山海牙懷印綬去，得免。

translations.literal: One son, Gui Shanhaiya, fled carrying the seals and ribbons and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui Shanhaiya fled with the official seals and survived.

sentences.zh: 明安達爾，唐兀氏，字士元，炳同年進士，由宿州判官再轉為潛江云。

translations.literal: Mingandár, of the Tangut clan, style name Shiyuan, was a jinshi in the same year as Bing; from judge of Suzhou he was again transferred to darughachi of Qianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mingandár, a Tangut whose style name was Shiyuan, had passed the jinshi in the same year as Bing. He rose from judge of Suzhou to darughachi of Qianjiang.

sentences.zh: 劉耕孫，字存吾，茶陵州人。

translations.literal: Liu Gengsun, style name Cunwu, was a man of Chaling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gengsun, whose style name was Cunwu, came from Chaling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至順元年進士，授承事郎、桂陽路臨武縣尹。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Zhishun, he was appointed court gentleman and magistrate of Linwu County in Guiyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of 1330, he was appointed court gentleman and magistrate of Linwu County in Guiyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 臨武近蠻獠，耕孫至，召父老告之曰：「吾儒士也，今為汝邑尹，爾父老當體吾教，訓其子弟，孝弟力田，暇則事《詩》、 《書》，毋自棄以乾吾政。」

translations.literal: Linwu was near the Man and Liao peoples. When Gengsun arrived he summoned the elders and told them: "I am a Confucian scholar; now I am your prefectural magistrate—you elders should embody my teaching, instruct your sons and younger brothers in filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming, and in leisure attend to the Odes and Documents; do not abandon yourselves and interfere with my administration."
translations.idiomatic: Linwu lay near Man and Liao territory. On arriving, Gengsun summoned the elders and said, "I am a Confucian scholar and now your magistrate. Teach your sons filial piety, fraternal duty, and diligent farming. In their spare time let them study the Odes and Documents. Do not neglect yourselves and thwart my rule."

sentences.zh: 乃為建學校，求民間俊秀教之，設俎豆，習禮讓，三年文化大興。

translations.literal: He then built a school, sought outstanding talent among the people to teach them, set out sacrificial vessels, and practiced ritual and deference; within three years culture flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He built schools, recruited talented locals to teach, established ritual observances, and within three years transformed the district.

sentences.zh: 邑有茶課，歲不過五錠，後增至五十錠，耕孫言於朝，除其額。

translations.literal: The district had a tea levy, yearly not exceeding five ingots; later it increased to fifty ingots. Gengsun spoke to the court and removed this quota.
translations.idiomatic: The district's tea tax had been five ingots a year but rose to fifty. Gengsun petitioned the court and had the quota reduced.

sentences.zh: 歷建德、徽州、瑞州三路推官，所至詳讞疑獄，其政績卓然者甚眾。

translations.literal: He served successively as judicial officer of Jiande, Huizhou, and Ruizhou circuits; wherever he went he examined doubtful cases in detail, and his political achievements that stood out were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial officer in Jiande, Huizhou, and Ruizhou circuits, examining doubtful cases wherever he went and earning a distinguished record.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年春，蘄黃賊攻破湖南。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year of Zhizheng, Qi-Huang bandits broke through and overran Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1352, Qi-Huang rebels overran Hunan.

sentences.zh: 耕孫傾家貲募義丁，以援茶陵，賊至輒卻，故茶陵久不失守。

translations.literal: Gengsun poured out his family wealth to recruit righteous soldiers to relieve Chaling; whenever bandits came they were repelled, and therefore Chaling long did not lose its defense.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsun spent his family fortune to raise militia for Chaling. Whenever rebels came they were driven back, and Chaling held for a long time.

sentences.zh: 十五年，轉儒林郎、寧國路推官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Confucian gentleman and judicial officer of Ningguo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1355 he was made Confucian gentleman and judicial officer of Ningguo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，勸富民發粟賑之，活者萬計。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he urged wealthy families to distribute grain for relief; those who lived numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine he persuaded wealthy families to distribute grain, saving tens of thousands of lives.

sentences.zh: 會長槍瑣南班、程述、謝璽等攻寧國，耕孫分守城西南，日署府事，夜率兵乘城固守。

translations.literal: When the long-spear leader Suonanban, Cheng Shu, Xie Xi, and others attacked Ningguo, Gengsun divided forces to defend the city's southwest, by day signing prefectural documents and by night leading troops to mount the wall and hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel leaders Suonanban, Cheng Shu, and Xie Xi attacked Ningguo, Gengsun held the southwest quarter, handling prefectural affairs by day and leading troops on the walls by night.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省遣參知政事吉尼哥兒來援，至則兵已疲矣。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat sent associate administrator Jinige'er to relieve them; when he arrived the troops were already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat sent associate administrator Jinige'er to relieve them, but by the time he arrived the defenders were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 城恃有援，不為備。

translations.literal: The city relied on having reinforcements and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The city, trusting in relief, let its guard down.

sentences.zh: 瑣南班知之，夜四鼓，引眾緣堞而上，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Suonanban knew this; at the fourth watch of the night he led the multitude up along the parapet, and the city thereupon fell.
translations.idiomatic: Suonanban learned of this. At the fourth watch he led his men up the parapet, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 耕孫力戰遇害。

translations.literal: Gengsun fought fiercely and met with disaster and death.
translations.idiomatic: Gengsun fought on until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 弟燾孫，以國學生下第，授常寧州儒學正。

translations.literal: His younger brother Taosun, having failed the Imperial Academy examination, was appointed Confucian director of Changning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Taosun, having failed the Imperial Academy examination, was appointed Confucian director of Changning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 湖南陷，常寧長吏棄城走，民奉印請燾孫為城守，城賴以完者一年。

translations.literal: When Hunan fell, the chief officials of Changning abandoned the city and fled; the people presented the seal and asked Taosun to defend the city, and the city relied on this to remain intact for one year.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan fell, Changning's officials fled. The people begged Taosun to hold the city, and it remained secure for a year.

sentences.zh: 外援俱絕，死之。

translations.literal: External relief was all cut off, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When all outside aid failed, he died defending it.

sentences.zh: 長子碩，為武昌江夏縣魯湖大使，起義兵援茶陵，亦死之。

translations.literal: The eldest son Shuo served as envoy of Lu Lake in Jiangxia County, Wuchang; he raised righteous troops to relieve Chaling and also died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shuo, an official at Lu Lake in Jiangxia, raised militia to aid Chaling and was also killed.

sentences.zh: 俞述祖，字紹芳，慶元象山人。

translations.literal: Yu Shuzu, style name Shaofang, was a man of Xiangshan in Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shuzu, whose style name was Shaofang, came from Xiangshan in Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 由翰林書寫考滿，調廣東元帥府都事，入為國史院編修官，已而出為沔陽府推官。

translations.literal: Having passed the Hanlin copyist examination with full marks, he was transferred to chief clerk of the Guangdong Marshal's Office, entered as historiographer of the National History Institute, and then went out as judicial officer of Mianyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the Hanlin copyist examination, he served as chief clerk of the Guangdong Marshal's Office, then as historiographer at the National History Institute, and finally as judicial officer of Mianyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，蘄黃賊迫州境，述祖領民兵守綠水洪，並力捍御之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, Qi-Huang bandits pressed the prefectural border; Shuzu led militia to defend Lüshui Ford and together strove to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352, Qi-Huang rebels threatened Mianyang. Shuzu led militia to defend Lüshui Ford.

sentences.zh: 兵力不支，沔陽城陷，民兵悉潰。

translations.literal: Military strength could not hold; Mianyang city fell and the militia all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When strength failed, Mianyang fell and the militia scattered.

sentences.zh: 述祖為賊所執，械至其偽主徐壽輝所，誘之使降。

translations.literal: Shuzu was seized by bandits, shackled and brought to their false lord Xu Shouhui, who enticed him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu was captured, bound, and brought before the rebel leader Xu Shouhui, who tried to win him over.

sentences.zh: 述祖罵不輟，壽輝怒，支解之。

translations.literal: Shuzu cursed without pause; Shouhui was enraged and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu cursed without cease. Shouhui in his fury had him dismembered.

sentences.zh: 有子方五歲，亦死。

translations.literal: He had a son five years old who also died.
translations.idiomatic: His five-year-old son was also killed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈奉訓大夫、禮部郎中、象山縣男。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Instructor of the Court, director of the Ministry of Rites, and Baron of Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously granted him Instructor of the Court, director of the Ministry of Rites, and the title Baron of Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 桂完澤者，永嘉人。

translations.literal: Gui Wanzhe was a man of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Wanzhe came from Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 嘗從江西左丞李朵兒留京師，得為平江路管軍鎮撫，為仇家所訴，免官。

translations.literal: He once followed the Jiangxi left vice censor Li Duo'er to remain in the capital and obtained the post of military pacification commissioner of Pingjiang Circuit; he was impeached by an enemy family and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed Jiangxi left vice censor Li Duo'er to the capital and been appointed military pacification commissioner of Pingjiang Circuit, but enemies impeached him and he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 會賊攻昱嶺關，行省遂假前官，令從征。

translations.literal: When bandits attacked Yuling Pass, the branch secretariat thereupon lent him his former office and ordered him to follow the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Yuling Pass, the branch secretariat restored his former rank and sent him to campaign.

sentences.zh: 完澤勇於討賊，凡再戰關下，皆勝。

translations.literal: Wanzhe was brave in pursuing bandits; twice he fought below the pass and both times won.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhe fought bravely against the rebels and twice defeated them below the pass.

sentences.zh: 尋又與賊鬥，為所執，其妻弟金德亦被擒，皆反縛於樹，臨以白刃，脅之降。

translations.literal: Shortly he again fought the bandits and was seized; his wife's younger brother Jin De was also captured; both were bound backward to trees, faced with naked blades, and coerced to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again and was captured, along with his brother-in-law Jin De. Both were bound to trees, blades at their throats, and ordered to submit.

sentences.zh: 金德意未決，完澤呼曰：「金舅，男子漢即死，不可聽賊。」

translations.literal: Jin De's intention was undecided; Wanzhe called out: "Uncle Jin, a true man dies at once—do not listen to the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Jin De hesitated. Wanzhe called out, "Uncle Jin, a real man dies once—do not heed these rebels."

sentences.zh: 德曰：「此言最是。」

translations.literal: De said: "These words are most correct."
translations.idiomatic: Jin De replied, "You speak the truth."

sentences.zh: 因大罵。

translations.literal: He thereupon cursed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: They cursed the rebels together.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，剖二人之腹而死。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and disemboweled the two men to death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in their fury cut open their bellies and killed them.

sentences.zh: 醜閭，字時中，蒙古氏。

translations.literal: Choulu, style name Shizhong, was of the Mongol clan.
translations.idiomatic: Choulu, whose style name was Shizhong, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 登元統元年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1333.

sentences.zh: 累官京畿漕運副使，出知安陸府。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to vice commissioner of capital grain transport and went out as prefect of Anlu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice commissioner of capital grain transport, then was appointed prefect of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，蘄賊曾法興犯安陸，時醜閭募兵得數百人，帥以拒賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng, Qi bandit Zeng Faxing invaded Anlu; at that time Choulu recruited troops and obtained several hundred men, leading them to resist the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 the Qi rebel Zeng Faxing attacked Anlu. Choulu raised several hundred men and led them against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敗賊前隊，乘勝追之。

translations.literal: He defeated the bandits' vanguard and pursued them in victory.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebel vanguard and pursued in victory.

sentences.zh: 而賊自他門入，亟還兵，則城中火起，軍民潰亂，計不可遏，乃歸，服朝服，出坐公堂。

translations.literal: But the bandits entered through another gate; he hastily returned with troops, yet fires had risen in the city, soldiers and civilians scattered in disorder, the situation could not be checked, and he therefore returned, donned court robes, and came out to sit in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: But rebels entered through another gate. He rushed back to find the city ablaze and troops in chaos. Seeing nothing could be done, he put on his court robes and sat in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 賊脅以白刃，醜閭猶喻以逆順。

translations.literal: The bandits coerced him with naked blades; Choulu still lectured them on rebellion and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threatened him with blades, yet he still lectured them on loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 一賊排醜閭下，使拜，不屈，且怒罵。

translations.literal: One bandit pushed Choulu down and made him bow; he would not yield and moreover cursed angrily.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel forced him down to bow. He refused and cursed them.

sentences.zh: 賊酋不忍害，拘之。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain could not bear to harm him and detained him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief spared him for the moment and held him captive.

sentences.zh: 明日，又逼其從亂，醜閭疾叱曰：「吾守土臣，寧從汝賊乎！」

translations.literal: The next day they again forced him to join the disorder; Choulu sharply rebuked them: "I am a minister who guards the soil—would I follow you bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day they pressed him to join them. Choulu snapped, "I am a guardian of this land. Would I follow you rebels?"

sentences.zh: 賊怒，以刀斫醜閭左脅，斷而死。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and hacked Choulu's left flank with a blade, severing him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hacked his left side and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊憤其不降，復以布囊囊其屍，舁置其家。

translations.literal: The bandits resented that he would not submit; they again placed his corpse in a cloth sack and carried it to set before his house.
translations.idiomatic: Angry that he would not yield, they stuffed his corpse in a sack and dumped it at his door.

sentences.zh: 醜閭妻侯氏出，大哭，且列酒肉滿前，渴者令飲酒，飢者令食肉，以紿賊之不防己。

translations.literal: Choulu's wife Lady Hou came out, wailed greatly, and moreover set out wine and meat in full before them, letting the thirsty drink wine and the hungry eat meat, to deceive the bandits into not guarding against her.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Hou came out wailing, then set out wine and meat for the rebels—feeding the thirsty and hungry to lull their watchfulness.

sentences.zh: 至夜，自經死。

translations.literal: By night she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: That night she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈醜閭河南行省參知政事，贈侯氏寧夏郡夫人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Choulu was posthumously granted associate administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Lady Hou was granted Lady of Ningxia Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made Choulu associate administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat and Lady Hou Lady of Ningxia Commandery.

sentences.zh: 立表其門曰雙節。

translations.literal: A tablet was erected at their gate reading "Double Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: A tablet reading "Double Integrity" was erected at their gate.

sentences.zh: 有馮三者，湖廣省一公使也，素不知書。

translations.literal: There was one Feng San, a first-class messenger of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, who by nature did not know books.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Feng San, a first-class messenger of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, who could not read.

sentences.zh: 湖廣為寇陷，皁隸輩悉起，剽殺為盜，亦拉三以從。

translations.literal: When Huguang was overrun by bandits, the runners and attendants all rose up, plundering and killing to become bandits, and also dragged San along with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huguang fell to rebels, clerks and runners turned to plunder and tried to drag San along.

sentences.zh: 三辭曰：「賊名惡，我等豈可為！」

translations.literal: San declined, saying: "The name of bandit is vile—how could we do this!"
translations.idiomatic: San refused. "Banditry is a foul name," he said. "How can we do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 眾初強之，終弗從，怒將殺之，三遂唾罵。

translations.literal: At first the multitude forced him strongly, but in the end he would not follow; enraged, they were about to kill him, and San thereupon spat and cursed.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him hard, but he would not yield. Enraged, they were about to kill him, and he spat and cursed them.

sentences.zh: 賊乃縛諸十字木，舁之以行，而刲其肉，三益罵不止。

translations.literal: The bandits thereupon bound him to a cross-shaped wooden frame, carried him as they went, and sliced his flesh; San cursed all the more without cease.
translations.idiomatic: They bound him to a cross, carried him along, and sliced his flesh as they went. He only cursed louder.

sentences.zh: 抵江上，斷其喉，委去。

translations.literal: Reaching the riverbank, they cut his throat and cast him away.
translations.idiomatic: At the river they cut his throat and cast him aside.

sentences.zh: 其妻隨三號泣，俯拾刲肉，納布裙中。

translations.literal: His wife followed San, wailing; she stooped to pick up the sliced flesh and put it in her cloth skirt.
translations.idiomatic: His wife followed, wailing, and gathered the sliced flesh into her skirt.

sentences.zh: 伺賊遠，收三血骸，脫衣裹之，大泣，投江而死。

translations.literal: When the bandits were far off, she collected San's bloody remains, removed her clothes to wrap them, wept greatly, and threw herself into the river to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were gone, she gathered his remains, wrapped them in her clothes, and threw herself into the river.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒，字國賓，高昌人。

translations.literal: Bolu Temür, style name Guobin, was a man of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu Temür, whose style name was Guobin, came from Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 由宿衛補官，十三轉而為江東廉訪副使。

translations.literal: From palace guard he filled offices; after thirteen transfers he became vice censor of the Jiangdong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a palace guard, he rose through thirteen posts to vice censor of the Jiangdong surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 以選為襄陽路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: By selection he was appointed darughachi of Xiangyang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as darughachi of Xiangyang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 至正十一年，盜起汝、潁，均州鄖縣人田端子等亦聚眾殺官吏，孛羅帖木兒將民兵捕斬之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhizheng bandits arose in Ru and Ying; the men of Yun County in Jun Prefecture, Tian Duanzi and others, also gathered crowds to kill officials. Bolu Temür led militia to capture and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 rebels rose in Ru and Ying. In Jun Prefecture, Tian Duanzi and others gathered mobs and killed officials. Bolu Temür led militia to capture and execute them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，行省、廉訪司同檄孛羅帖木兒，以其所領兵會諸軍於均、房同討賊，賊始退。

translations.literal: Before long the branch secretariat and surveillance commission jointly issued orders to Bolu Temür to lead his troops to join the various armies at Jun and Fang to subdue bandits together; the bandits thereupon retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the branch secretariat and surveillance commission ordered him to join forces at Jun and Fang. The rebels retreated.

sentences.zh: 而谷城、光化以急告，即帥兵趨谷城，而分遣樊城主簿脫因等趨光化，且遣使求糧於襄陽，不應；

translations.literal: But Gucheng and Guanghua reported urgent distress; he immediately led troops toward Gucheng, while dispatching Fancheng registrar Tuoyin and others toward Guanghua, and also sent envoys to seek grain at Xiangyang—no response;
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng and Guanghua sent urgent appeals. He marched at once for Gucheng, sent Fancheng registrar Tuoyin and others toward Guanghua, and requested grain from Xiangyang—without success.

sentences.zh: 遣同知也先不花促之，又不應。

translations.literal: He sent associate administrator Yexian Buhua to urge them, and again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: He sent associate administrator Yexian Buhua to press the matter, again without response.

sentences.zh: 軍乏食，不能行，乃駐於柴店。

translations.literal: The army lacked food and could not march, and therefore encamped at Chaidian.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies ran out and the army could not move, so they halted at Chaidian.

sentences.zh: 復遣從子馬哈失力往告，詞甚苦切。

translations.literal: He again sent his nephew Mahashili to report, his words very bitter and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his nephew Mahashili with an urgent, desperate appeal.

sentences.zh: 廉訪分司王僉事、本路總管柴順禮怒其責望，械之。

translations.literal: Surveillance sub-commissioner Wang and circuit intendant Chai Shunli were angry at his reproaches and shackled him.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance officer Wang and intendant Chai Shunli, angered by his demands, had him shackled.

sentences.zh: 適紐真來獻光化所獲首級，且言：「孛羅帖木兒在谷城與賊相持，未知存歿，宜急濟其糧，少緩，恐弗及矣。」

translations.literal: Just then Niuzhen came to present heads taken at Guanghua and said: "Bolu Temür is at Gucheng locked in combat with bandits; whether he lives or dies is unknown. Grain should be rushed to him—delay a little and it may be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Niuzhen arrived with heads from Guanghua and reported, "Bolu Temür is fighting at Gucheng. His fate is unknown. Send grain at once—or it may be too late."

sentences.zh: 於是脫二人械，遣還，而命也先不花與萬戶也先帖木耳率數千人，會孛羅帖木兒以討賊。

translations.literal: They thereupon released the two men from shackles and sent them back, and ordered Yexian Buhua and commander Yexian Temür to lead several thousand men to join Bolu Temür in subduing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The two messengers were freed and sent back. Yexian Buhua and commander Yexian Temür were ordered to lead several thousand men to join Bolu Temür.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，襄陽失守，也先不花等聞之驚潰。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Xiangyang was lost; Yexian Buhua and others, hearing this, fled in panic and collapse.
translations.idiomatic: The next January Xiangyang fell. Yexian Buhua and his troops broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒領義兵二百人，且戰且引至監利縣，遇沔陽府達魯花赤咬住、同知三山、安陸府同知燕只不花、荊襄提舉相哥失力之師。

translations.literal: Bolu Temür led two hundred righteous soldiers, fighting as he withdrew to Jianli County, and met the troops of Mianyang darughachi Qiaozhu, associate administrator Sanshan, Anlu associate administrator Yanzhibuhua, and Jing-Xiang commissioner Xianggeshili.
translations.idiomatic: Bolu Temür led two hundred militiamen, fighting as he withdrew to Jianli, where he joined forces with Mianyang darughachi Qiaozhu, associate administrator Sanshan, Anlu associate administrator Yanzhibuhua, and Jing-Xiang commissioner Xianggeshili.

sentences.zh: 時濱江有船千餘，乃糾合諸義兵丁壯水工五千餘人，畀以軍號，給以刀槊，具哨馬五十，水陸繼進。

translations.literal: At that time along the riverbank there were more than a thousand boats; he therefore gathered righteous soldiers, sturdy youths, and water workers—more than five thousand—gave them military designations, supplied spears and blades, provided fifty scout horses, and advanced by land and water in succession.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand boats lay along the river. He gathered five thousand militiamen and boatmen, armed them, provided fifty scouts, and advanced by land and water.

sentences.zh: 比至石首縣，聞中興路亦陷，乃議趨岳州就元帥帖桀，而道阻不得前，仍趨襄陽。

translations.literal: When they reached Shishou County they heard that Zhongxing Circuit had also fallen; they then discussed hurrying to Yuezhou to join Marshal Tieji, but the road was blocked and they could not advance, and still pressed toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Shishou they learned Zhongxing had fallen. They tried to reach Marshal Tieji at Yuezhou but the route was blocked and they turned again toward Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 賊方駐楊湖港，乘其不虞擊之，獲其船二十七艘，生擒賊黨劉咬兒。

translations.literal: The bandits were encamped at Yanghu Harbor; taking them unawares they struck, capturing twenty-seven of their boats and taking alive the bandit Liu Yao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were at Yanghu Harbor. Catching them off guard, they seized twenty-seven boats and captured Liu Yao'er alive.

sentences.zh: 訊得其情，進次潛江縣，又斬賊數百級，獲三十餘船，梟賊將劉萬戶、許堂主等。

translations.literal: Interrogating him they learned the situation; advancing to Qianjiang County they again beheaded several hundred bandits, captured more than thirty boats, and displayed the heads of bandit generals Liu Wanhu, Xu Tangzhu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: From his interrogation they advanced to Qianjiang, killed hundreds more, took thirty boats, and executed rebel commanders Liu Wanhu and Xu Tangzhu.

sentences.zh: 是日，甫止兵未食而賊大至，與戰抵暮，咬住等軍各當一面，不能救。

translations.literal: That day, having just halted the troops without eating, bandits arrived in force; they fought until evening. Qiaozhu and the others each held one face and could not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: That day they had barely halted to eat when rebels came in force. They fought until evening while Qiaozhu's detachments, each holding a separate front, could not help.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒被重創，麾馬哈失力使去，曰：「吾以死報國，汝無留此。」

translations.literal: Bolu Temür received grave wounds and directed Mahashili to leave, saying: "I repay the state with death—you must not stay here."
translations.idiomatic: Bolu Temür was gravely wounded and ordered Mahashili away. "I die for the state," he said. "Do not stay."

sentences.zh: 馬哈失力泣曰：「死生從叔父。」

translations.literal: Mahashili wept and said: "Life and death follow my uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Mahashili wept, "Life and death—I follow my uncle."

sentences.zh: 既而孛羅帖木兒被執，賊請同為逆，孛羅帖木兒怒罵之，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Before long Bolu Temür was seized; the bandits asked him to join in rebellion together; Bolu Temür cursed them angrily and thereupon met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bolu Temür was captured. The rebels asked him to join them. He cursed them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 馬哈失力帥家奴求其屍，復與賊戰，俱沒於陣。

translations.literal: Mahashili led household slaves to seek his corpse, again fought the bandits, and all perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Mahashili led household slaves to recover the body, fought the rebels again, and all died in battle.

sentences.zh: 舉家死者，凡二十六人。

translations.literal: Those of the whole family who died numbered twenty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six members of the family died in all.

sentences.zh: 彭庭堅，字允誠，溫州瑞安人。

translations.literal: Peng Tingjian, style name Yuncheng, was a man of Ruian in Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Tingjian, whose style name was Yuncheng, came from Ruian in Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢至正四年進士第，授承事郎、同知沂州事。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi examination of the fourth year of Zhizheng and appointed court gentleman and associate administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1344 and was appointed court gentleman and associate administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 毀牛皇神祠，驅鄰郡上馬賊，免民橫急徵斂，民甚便之。

translations.literal: He destroyed the Ox Emperor spirit shrine, drove off horse-bandits from neighboring prefectures, and exempted the people from harsh urgent levies—the people were greatly benefited.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed a superstitious shrine, drove off neighboring horse-thieves, and eased harsh levies—the people were greatly relieved.

sentences.zh: 俄以平反獄囚忤上官意，遂棄去。

translations.literal: Shortly, because he reversed wrongful convictions of prisoners and offended his superiors' intent, he thereupon abandoned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reversed wrongful convictions, offended his superiors, and resigned.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔選守令，以建寧路崇安縣尹起庭堅於家。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict selected prefects and magistrates; he was summoned from home to be magistrate of Chong'an County in Jianning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1350 an edict called for local officials; he was summoned from home as magistrate of Chong'an in Jianning.

sentences.zh: 屬鉛山寇周良竊發，犯閩關，庭堅御之有法，寇不入境。

translations.literal: When the Qianshan bandit Zhou Liang rose in secret and invaded the Min Pass, Tingjian defended with method and the bandits did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit Zhou Liang of Qianshan raided the Min Pass, Tingjian held him off and kept the rebels out.

sentences.zh: 十一年，升同知建寧路總管府事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to associate administrator of the Jianning Circuit intendant's office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1351 he was promoted to associate administrator of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 江西寇熾，庭堅率民兵克復建陽，又進兵平浦城。

translations.literal: Jiangxi bandits were fierce; Tingjian led militia to recover Jianyang and advanced troops to pacify Pucheng.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiangxi rebels grew fierce, he led militia to recover Jianyang and pacify Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，攝僉都元帥府事，與邵武路總管吳按攤不花夾攻邵武，庭堅設雲梯火砲，晝夜攻擊，寇遁，追斬渠凶董元帥、鐵和尚、童昌，邵武悉平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he acted as deputy commander of the commander-in-chief's office; together with Shaowu intendant Wu Antan Buhua he attacked Shaowu from both sides. Tingjian set scaling ladders and fire cannon, attacking day and night; the bandits fled, and in pursuit he beheaded the ringleaders Commander Dong, Iron Monk, and Tong Chang—Shaowu was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 he acted as deputy commander and, with Shaowu intendant Wu Antan Buhua, assaulted Shaowu with scaling ladders and cannon day and night. The rebels fled; he pursued and killed ringleaders Commander Dong, Iron Monk, and Tong Chang, pacifying Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 總兵官江浙參政章嘉上功於朝，升同知福建道宣慰使司副都元帥，鎮邵武。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief, Jiang-Zhe associate administrator Zhang Jia, reported merit to the court; he was promoted to associate deputy commander of the Fujian Branch Pacification Commission and garrisoned Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhang Jia reported his merits. He was made associate deputy commander of the Fujian pacification commission and garrisoned Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 冬，寇陷建寧縣。

translations.literal: In winter the bandits overran Jianning County.
translations.idiomatic: That winter rebels seized Jianning County.

sentences.zh: 十三年，庭堅統建陽、崇安、浦城三縣民兵，次泰宁。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Tingjian commanded militia of Jianyang, Chong'an, and Pucheng, and encamped at Taining.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353 he commanded militia from Jianyang, Chong'an, and Pucheng and encamped at Taining.

sentences.zh: 寇懼請降，復建寧縣，還師邵武。

translations.literal: The bandits feared and asked to surrender; he recovered Jianning County and returned his army to Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sued for peace. He recovered Jianning and returned to Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省檄庭堅節制建寧、邵武二郡諸軍。

translations.literal: The Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat ordered Tingjian to command all armies of the two prefectures Jianning and Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiang-Zhe secretariat placed him in command of all forces in Jianning and Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 十四年，盜侵政和、松溪，江南行台中丞吳鐸督軍建寧，檄庭堅至。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits invaded Zhenghe and Songxi; Jiangnan Branch Censor Wu Duo supervised troops at Jianning and summoned Tingjian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 rebels invaded Zhenghe and Songxi. Censor Wu Duo summoned Tingjian to Jianning.

sentences.zh: 時鎮撫萬戶岳煥隸麾下，煥素悍，縱卒為暴，庭堅欲繩以法，煥懼，使部卒乘其不備，詐為賊兵，突入交鋒，眾皆潰，庭堅獨留不去，遂遇害，死年四十三。

translations.literal: At that time pacification commander Yue Huan was under his command; Huan was by nature fierce and let his soldiers run wild. Tingjian wished to bind him by law; Huan feared this and had his troops, taking him unawares, feign to be bandit soldiers and burst in to clash; the multitude all scattered, but Tingjian alone remained and would not leave, and thereupon met with disaster and death, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commander Yue Huan served under him, a brutal man whose troops ran wild. When Tingjian moved to discipline him, Huan had his men feign a rebel attack. The army broke; Tingjian alone stood his ground and was killed at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 故吏張椿，儒士夏志行、江晃，奉柩還崇安，民哀泣如喪父母，立祠像，歲時祭禱，數降靈響，旁邑立祠亦如之。

translations.literal: Former clerk Zhang Chun and scholars Xia Zhixing and Jiang Huang escorted the coffin back to Chong'an; the people wept as if mourning parents, erected shrine images, and prayed at the seasons; spirit sounds descended many times, and neighboring districts likewise erected shrines.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhang Chun and scholars Xia Zhixing and Jiang Huang brought his coffin home. The people mourned as for parents, built shrines, and reported spirit manifestations; neighboring districts did the same.

sentences.zh: 南行台監察御史餘觀行部巡察，獲其賊斬之。

translations.literal: Southern Branch investigating censor Yu Guan toured on inspection and captured the murderer and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Branch censor Yu Guan investigated and executed the killer.

sentences.zh: 為上其事，贈中奉大夫、福建道宣慰使都元帥，封忠愍侯。

translations.literal: Reporting the matter upward, he was posthumously granted junior grand master of the court, commander-in-chief of the Fujian Pacification Commission, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him junior grand master of the court, commander-in-chief of Fujian, and Marquis of Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 王伯顏，字伯敬，濱州沾化人。

translations.literal: Wang Boyan, style name Bojing, was a man of Zhanhua in Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boyan, whose style name was Bojing, came from Zhanhua in Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 由湖廣省宣使歷永州祁陽、湖州烏程縣尹，信州推官。

translations.literal: From Huguang Branch Secretariat envoy he served successively as magistrate of Qiyang in Yongzhou and Wucheng in Huzhou, and as judicial officer of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Huguang secretariat envoy he served as magistrate of Qiyang and Wucheng and as judicial officer of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 至正九年，遷知福寧州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhizheng he was transferred to prefect of Funing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1349 he was made prefect of Funing.
