sentences.zh: 居三歲，升福建鹽運副使，將行，憲府以時方俶擾，留伯顏仍領州事。

translations.literal: After three years he was promoted to vice commissioner of Fujian salt transport; about to depart, the surveillance commission, because the times were turbulent, kept Boyan still in charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was promoted to Fujian salt transport vice commissioner, but unrest kept him at his prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊自邵武間道逼福寧，乃與監州阿撒都剌募壯兵五萬，分扼險阻。

translations.literal: Before long bandits by a secret route from Shaowu pressed Funing; he together with supervising prefect Asadula recruited fifty thousand sturdy troops and divided them to hold strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels from Shaowu threatened Funing by a hidden route. He and supervising prefect Asadula raised fifty thousand men to hold the passes.

sentences.zh: 賊至楊梅嶺，立柵，伯顏與子相馳破之。

translations.literal: When bandits reached Yangmei Ridge and set up palisades, Boyan and his son Xiang charged and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangmei Ridge the rebels built palisades; Boyan and his son Xiang broke them in a charge.

sentences.zh: 賊帥王善，俄擁眾直壓州西門，胥隸皆解散，伯顏麾下唯白梃市兒數百人爾。

translations.literal: Bandit chieftain Wang Shan shortly gathered crowds and pressed straight upon the prefecture's west gate; clerks and runners all dispersed; under Boyan there were only several hundred market youths with white staves.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Wang Shan soon pressed the west gate. Clerks fled; Boyan had only a few hundred men with clubs.

sentences.zh: 伯顏射賊，不復反顧，賊以長槍舂馬，馬僕，遂見執。

translations.literal: Boyan shot at bandits without turning back; bandits used long spears to ram his horse; the horse fell, and he was thereupon seized.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan shot at the enemy without looking back. Spearmen struck down his horse and seized him.

sentences.zh: 善說伯顏曰：「聞公有惠政，此州那可無尹，公為我尹，可乎？」

translations.literal: Shan persuaded Boyan, saying: "I hear you have benevolent administration—this prefecture cannot be without a prefect; will you be prefect for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Shan said, "Your rule has won the people. This prefecture needs you. Serve as our prefect—will you?"

sentences.zh: 伯顏訶善曰：「我天子命官，不幸失守，義當死，肯從汝反乎？」

translations.literal: Boyan rebuked Shan: "I am an officer appointed by the Son of Heaven; unluckily I lost the defense—righteousness demands death; would I follow you in rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: Boyan rebuked him, "I am the Son of Heaven's officer. I have lost the city and should die. Would I rebel with you?"

sentences.zh: 善怒，叱左右搤以跪，弗屈，遂毆之。

translations.literal: Shan was enraged and ordered those beside him to force him to kneel; he would not yield and they thereupon beat him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan in rage had him forced to his knees. He would not yield and they beat him.

sentences.zh: 伯顏嚼舌出血噀善面，罵曰；

translations.literal: Boyan chewed his tongue until blood came out and spat it on Shan's face, cursing:
translations.idiomatic: Boyan bit his tongue, spat blood in Shan's face, and cursed:

sentences.zh: 「反賊，殺即殺，何以毆為！

translations.literal: "Rebel traitors—if you kill, then kill; why beat!
translations.idiomatic: "Traitors—kill me if you will. Why beat me?

sentences.zh: 吾民天民也，汝不可害。

translations.literal: My people are the people of Heaven—you must not harm them.
translations.idiomatic: My people belong to Heaven. You must not harm them.

sentences.zh: 大丞相親討叛逆，百萬之師，雷擊電掃，汝輩小丑，將無遺種，顧敢爾邪！」

translations.literal: The grand chancellor personally campaigns against rebellion with an army of a million—thunder strike and lightning sweep—you petty clowns will leave no seed; how dare you act thus!"
translations.idiomatic: The grand chancellor leads a million men against you. You vermin will be wiped out. How dare you!"

sentences.zh: 賊亦執阿撒都剌至，善厲聲責其拒鬥，噤不能對。

translations.literal: The bandits also seized Asadula; Shan sternly rebuked him for resisting battle, and he was silent and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Asadula too. Shan rebuked his resistance; he could not answer.

sentences.zh: 伯顏复唾善曰：「我殺賊，何言拒邪！

translations.literal: Boyan again spat on Shan: "I killed bandits—what talk of resistance!
translations.idiomatic: Boyan spat again. "I killed rebels—what resistance?

sentences.zh: 我死，當為神以殺汝。」

translations.literal: When I die I shall become a spirit to kill you."
translations.idiomatic: When I die I shall be a ghost and kill you."

sentences.zh: 言訖，挺頸受刃，頸斷，湧白液如乳。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he stretched his neck to receive the blade; his neck was severed and white fluid like milk gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: He offered his neck. When the blade fell, white fluid like milk poured forth.

sentences.zh: 暴屍數日，色不變，州人哭聲連巷。

translations.literal: His corpse was exposed several days without change of color; the people's cries of mourning filled the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: His body lay exposed for days unchanged; mourning filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 賊既殺阿撒都剌，欲釋相官之，相詈曰；

translations.literal: After the bandits had killed Asadula they wished to release Xiang and give him office; Xiang cursed:
translations.idiomatic: After killing Asadula they offered Xiang office. He cursed:

sentences.zh: 「吾與汝不共戴天，恨不寸斬汝，我受汝官邪！」

translations.literal: "I and you cannot live under the same sky—I regret only that I cannot cut you inch by inch—would I accept office from you!"
translations.idiomatic: "We cannot share the sky. I only regret I cannot hack you to bits. Would I take your office?"

sentences.zh: 賊殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed him.

sentences.zh: 相妻潘氏，挈二女，為賊所獲，亦罵賊，母子同死。

translations.literal: Xiang's wife Lady Pan, leading two daughters, was seized by bandits and also cursed them; mother and daughters died together.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Pan and two daughters were captured; they cursed the rebels and died together.

sentences.zh: 伯顏既死，賊時睹其引兵出入。

translations.literal: After Boyan had died, the bandits at times saw him leading troops in and out.
translations.idiomatic: After Boyan's death rebels sometimes saw him leading troops.

sentences.zh: 明年，州有僧林德誠者，起兵討賊，乃望空噓曰：「王州尹，王州尹，宜率陰兵助我斬賊。」

translations.literal: The next year there was a monk Lin Decheng in the prefecture who raised troops to subdue bandits; he therefore called to the empty sky: "Prefect Wang, Prefect Wang—you should lead yin soldiers to help me behead bandits."
translations.idiomatic: The next year monk Lin Decheng raised troops and called to the sky, "Prefect Wang, lead your ghost soldiers to help me destroy these rebels."

sentences.zh: 時賊正祠神，睹紅衣軍來，以為偽帥康將軍，亟往迎之，無有也，四面皆青衣官軍，賊大敗。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits were sacrificing to spirits and saw red-clad troops coming; they thought it was the false commander General Kang and hastened to welcome them, but there were none; on all four sides were green-clad government troops, and the bandits were greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, sacrificing to gods, saw red-clad troops and thought them allies—then green-clad government forces appeared on every side and routed them.

sentences.zh: 斬其酋江二蠻，福寧遂平。

translations.literal: They beheaded their chieftain Jiang E'man, and Funing thereupon was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded chief Jiang E'man and pacified Funing.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈嘉議大夫、濟南路總管、上輕車都尉，追封太原郡侯。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted grand master for court discussion, intendant of Jinan Circuit, senior commander of light chariots, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him grand master for court discussion, intendant of Jinan, senior commander of light chariots, and Marquis of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉濬，字濟川，其先興州人。

translations.literal: Liu Jun, style name Jichuan—his ancestors were men of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun, whose style name was Jichuan, was descended from Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖海，金進士第一人，仕至河南府尹，死於國難，子孫遂家河南。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hai was the first-ranked jinshi of the Jin, served to prefect of Henan, and died in the state's calamity; descendants thereupon made their home in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Hai was top jinshi of the Jin, rose to prefect of Henan, and died in the dynastic collapse; the family then settled in Henan.

sentences.zh: 濬由廉訪司書吏調連江縣寧善鄉巡檢。

translations.literal: Jun was transferred from surveillance commission clerk to inspector of Ningshan Township in Lianjiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Jun rose from surveillance clerk to inspector of Ningshan Township in Lianjiang County.

sentences.zh: 至正十三年，江西賊帥王善寇閩，官軍守羅源縣拒之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng, Jiangxi bandit chieftain Wang Shan invaded Min; government troops defended Luoyuan County to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353 Jiangxi rebel chief Wang Shan invaded Fujian; government troops held Luoyuan County.

sentences.zh: 羅源與連江接壤，勢將迫。

translations.literal: Luoyuan bordered Lianjiang and the momentum was about to press upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyuan bordered Lianjiang; the threat was imminent.

sentences.zh: 濬妻真定史氏，故相家女也，有才識，謂濬​​曰：「事急矣，可聚兵以捍一方。」

translations.literal: Jun's wife Lady Shi of Zhending, daughter of a former chancellor's family, had talent and insight; she said to Jun: "The matter is urgent—you can gather troops to defend one region."
translations.idiomatic: Jun's wife Lady Shi of Zhending, a former chancellor's daughter, urged him, "The crisis is upon us. Gather troops and defend this region."

sentences.zh: 於是盡出奩中物，募壯士百餘，命仲子健將之。

translations.literal: She thereupon brought out everything in her trousseau, recruited more than a hundred sturdy men, and ordered her second son Jian to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: She emptied her dowry to recruit a hundred warriors and sent their second son Jian to lead them.

sentences.zh: 浹旬間，眾至數万。

translations.literal: Within ten days the multitude reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days their force grew to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 賊尋破羅源，分兩道攻福州。

translations.literal: The bandits shortly broke Luoyuan and divided into two paths to attack Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon took Luoyuan and split to attack Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 濬拒之辰山，三戰三捷。

translations.literal: Jun resisted them at Chen Mountain—three battles, three victories.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held them at Chen Mountain with three victories.

sentences.zh: 俄聞福州陷，眾多潰去，濬獨帥健兵進。

translations.literal: Shortly word came that Fuzhou had fallen; the multitude mostly scattered and fled, but Jun alone led Jian's troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhou fell most troops fled, but Jun advanced with Jian's men alone.

sentences.zh: 遇賊於中麻，突其陣，斬前鋒五人，賊兵大至。

translations.literal: Meeting bandits at Zhongma, he burst into their formation and beheaded five vanguard men; bandit troops arrived in great force.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongma he broke the enemy line and killed five vanguard men before rebel masses arrived.

sentences.zh: 鏖戰三時頃，濬中箭墮馬，健下馬掖之，俱被獲。

translations.literal: Fierce battle lasted about three hours; Jun was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse; Jian dismounted to support him, and both were captured.
translations.idiomatic: After three hours of fighting Jun was shot from his horse. Jian dismounted to help him and both were taken.

sentences.zh: 濬忿，戟手大罵。

translations.literal: Jun was enraged and pointed with his hands while cursing loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Jun raged and cursed, pointing at them.

sentences.zh: 賊縛濬階下，先斫手一指，罵彌厲，再斫一指，亦如之。

translations.literal: The bandits bound Jun below the steps, first chopping off one finger of his hand; he cursed all the more fiercely, and again chopped one finger—the same.
translations.idiomatic: They bound him on the steps and cut off a finger. He cursed louder; they cut another.

sentences.zh: 指且盡，斫兩腕，次及兩足，濬色不少變，罵聲猶不絕，遂割其喉舌而死。

translations.literal: When his fingers were gone they chopped both wrists, then both feet; Jun's color changed not in the least, his curses still unceasing, and they thereupon cut his throat and tongue and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When his fingers were gone they severed his wrists, then his feet. His color never changed nor his curses ceased; they cut out his tongue and killed him.

sentences.zh: 健亦以死拒賊，善義之，舍健，使斂濬屍瘞之。

translations.literal: Jian also died resisting the bandits; Shan admired his righteousness, released Jian, and had him gather Jun's corpse and bury it.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died resisting. Shan admired his courage, spared him, and had him bury Jun.

sentences.zh: 健歸，請兵於帥府，以復父仇，弗聽。

translations.literal: Jian returned and asked the marshal's office for troops to avenge his father; they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sought troops from headquarters for revenge but was refused.

sentences.zh: 健盡散家貲，結死士百人，詐為工商流丐，入賊中，夜半，發火大噪，賊驚擾，自相​​屠戮，健手斬殺其父者張破四，並擒善及寇首陳伯祥來獻，磔之。

translations.literal: Jian spent all his family wealth, gathered a hundred men sworn to die, feigned to be merchants, laborers, and beggars, entered among the bandits, and at midnight set fires and raised a great clamor; the bandits were startled and disturbed and slaughtered one another; Jian with his own hand beheaded Zhang Posi, who had killed his father, and together captured Shan and bandit chieftain Chen Boxiang to present; they were dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Jian spent his fortune on a hundred men who infiltrated the camp as merchants and beggars. At midnight they raised fire and chaos. Jian slew Zhang Posi, who had killed his father, captured Shan and Chen Boxiang, and had them dismembered.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈濬福建行省檢校官，授健古田縣尹。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Jun was posthumously granted verifier of the Fujian Branch Secretariat, and Jian was appointed magistrate of Gutian County.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made Jun verifier of the Fujian secretariat and appointed Jian magistrate of Gutian.

sentences.zh: 官為濬立祠福州北門外，有司歲時致祭云。

translations.literal: The government erected a shrine to Jun outside Fuzhou's north gate; officials offered seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A shrine was built for Jun outside Fuzhou's north gate with seasonal sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 朵裡不花，字端甫，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Duolibuha, style name Duanfu, was a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Duolibuha, whose style name was Duanfu, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 始為宿衛官，累歷顯要，擢遼陽行省右丞，昇平章政事。

translations.literal: At first a palace guard officer, he rose through prominent posts to right vice censor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat and was elevated to grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a palace guard, rose to right vice censor of Liaoyang, and became grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒陷江西，詔拜江西行省平章政事，與平章政事阿兒渾沙等分道進討。

translations.literal: When Chen Youliang overran Jiangxi, an edict appointed him grand councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat; together with grand councillor Arhunsha and others he advanced by separate routes to pursue and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang seized Jiangxi, he was appointed Jiangxi grand councillor and marched with Arhunsha and others by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 遂泛海南下，趨廣東，駐師揭陽，降土寇金元祐，招复循、梅、惠三州之寇。

translations.literal: He thereupon sailed south on the sea toward Guangdong, encamped at Jieyang, subdued the local bandit Jin Yuanyou, and summoned back the bandits of Xun, Mei, and Hui prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed south to Guangdong, camped at Jieyang, subdued local bandit Jin Yuanyou, and recovered Xun, Mei, and Hui.

sentences.zh: 承製官其酋長，俾治賊以給兵食。

translations.literal: By imperial order he commissioned their chieftains and had them subdue bandits to supply army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He commissioned their chiefs to hunt rebels for army grain.

sentences.zh: 又別規粟四千石，輸送京師。

translations.literal: He also separately arranged four thousand piculs of grain and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent four thousand piculs of grain to the capital.

sentences.zh: 自是英、肇、欽、連諸郡皆附，且治兵由梅嶺以圖江西。

translations.literal: From this Ying, Zhao, Qin, and Lian prefectures all submitted, and he moreover trained troops to pass Meiling and plan for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Zhao, Qin, and Lian submitted. He trained troops to cross Meiling toward Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 而元祐有異志，託以鎮服其土，遮道固留。

translations.literal: But Yuanyou had ulterior intent, claiming to pacify his territory, blocking the road and firmly detaining him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou, however, harbored other designs and detained him on the road.

sentences.zh: 先是，制書命劉巨海僉廣東元帥府事，未發，元祐竊取，易其名，私畀徭賊劉文遠，誘與偕亂。

translations.literal: Earlier, an imperial order had appointed Liu Juhai to the Guangdong Marshal's Office; before it was issued Yuanyou stole it, changed the name, and privately gave it to the Yao bandit Liu Wenyuan, enticing him to join in disorder together.
translations.idiomatic: An order appointing Liu Juhai to the Guangdong marshal's office was stolen by Yuanyou, altered, and given to Yao rebel Liu Wenyuan to incite revolt.

sentences.zh: 事覺，文遠伏誅，而元祐及其弟元泰、子榮，竄匿不獲。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered Wenyuan was executed, but Yuanyou and his younger brother Yuantai and son Rong fled and hid and could not be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was executed, but Yuanyou, his brother Yuantai, and son Rong escaped.

sentences.zh: 俄榮率外賊突入，奪符信，殺官吏，變起倉卒，眾莫能支。

translations.literal: Shortly Rong led outside bandits in a sudden rush, seized seals and credentials, killed officials—the disturbance arose in sudden haste and the multitude could not withstand it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rong led outside rebels in, seized official seals, and killed officers before anyone could resist.

sentences.zh: 朵裡不花與參政楊泰元等，勒兵拒戰，而賊來益眾，朵裡不花為槍所中，創甚。

translations.literal: Duolibuha together with associate administrator Yang Taiyuan and others drove troops to resist battle, but bandits came in ever greater numbers; Duolibuha was struck by a spear and wounded severely.
translations.idiomatic: Duolibuha and associate administrator Yang Taiyuan fought back, but rebels swelled in number and Duolibuha was gravely wounded by a spear.

sentences.zh: 其子達蘭不花率麾下力與抗，死之。

translations.literal: His son Dalan Buhua led those under his command to strive in resistance and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dalan Buhua led his men in a last stand and was killed.

sentences.zh: 朵裡不花遂被執，擁至太平橋，罵不絕口，遂為賊殺。

translations.literal: Duolibuha was thereupon seized, dragged to Taiping Bridge, cursed without cease, and thereupon was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Duolibuha was seized, dragged to Taiping Bridge, cursed without pause, and killed.

sentences.zh: 其妻卜顏氏、妾高麗氏在側，不去，皆大罵曰：「我平章遇爾父子厚矣，爾父子何暴逆至此！」

translations.literal: His wife Lady Buyan and concubine Lady Gaoli were at his side and would not leave; both cursed loudly: "I, the grand councillor, treated you father and son generously—how could you father and son be so violent and rebellious to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Buyan and concubine Lady Gaoli stood by him and cursed, "The grand councillor treated you and your father well. How dare you rebel so viciously!"

sentences.zh: 亦皆遇害。

translations.literal: They also all met with disaster and death.
translations.idiomatic: They too were killed.

sentences.zh: 其部將哈乞、吳普顏、阿剌不花、歹不花等，俱戰死。

translations.literal: His subordinate generals Haqi, Wupuyan, Alabuhua, Daibuhua, and others all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Officers Haqi, Wupuyan, Alabuhua, Daibuhua, and others all fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 野峻台，其父世延，自有傳。

translations.literal: Ye Juntai—his father Shiyan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Juntai's father Shiyan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 由四川行省左右司郎中、西行台監察御史、河西廉訪使轉黃州路總管。

translations.literal: From left and right department director of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, Western Branch investigating censor, and Hexi surveillance commissioner he was transferred to intendant of Huangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from Sichuan secretariat director and Western Branch censor to Hexi surveillance commissioner, then intendant of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 湖廣既陷，朝廷察其材，升四川行省參政，命與平章咬住討賊。

translations.literal: When Huguang had fallen the court discerned his talent and elevated him to associate administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, ordering him together with grand councillor Qiaozhu to pursue and attack bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Huguang fell, the court promoted him to Sichuan associate administrator and ordered him with grand councillor Qiaozhu to fight rebels.

sentences.zh: 咬住軍五千，及分銳卒八百，使野峻台為前驅。

translations.literal: Qiaozhu's army was five thousand, and he divided eight hundred elite troops, making Ye Juntai the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaozhu had five thousand men and gave Ye Juntai eight hundred elite troops as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 賊方據巴東縣，攻拔之。

translations.literal: The bandits were holding Badong County; he attacked and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Badong County; he stormed and took it.

sentences.zh: 是時，歸、峽等州皆為賊所守，野峻台破賊江上，斬溺無算，已而歸、峽平。

translations.literal: At that time Gui, Xia, and other prefectures were all held by bandits; Ye Juntai defeated bandits on the river, beheading and drowning without number, and before long Gui and Xia were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and Xia prefectures were rebel-held. He routed them on the river with countless kills, then pacified both prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又進拔枝江、松滋兩縣，乘勝趨江陵。

translations.literal: He again advanced to take Zhijiang and Songzi counties and pressed in victory toward Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhijiang and Songzi and pressed on to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 賊出陣清水門，鏖戰至夕，賊退入城，乃據其門，俟咬住軍至。

translations.literal: The bandits deployed at Qingshui Gate; bitter battle lasted until evening; the bandits retreated into the city; he thereupon held the gate and waited for Qiaozhu's army to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels formed at Qingshui Gate. He fought until evening, drove them into the city, and held the gate for Qiaozhu.

sentences.zh: 黎明，賊出戰，三時頃，咬住軍止百步外，不救，賊飛槍刺之，​​遂死。

translations.literal: At dawn the bandits came out to battle; about three hours Qiaozhu's army halted a hundred paces away and did not rescue; bandits hurled flying spears and pierced him, and he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels sallied out. For three hours Qiaozhu's army stood a hundred paces off without helping. Flying spears struck Ye Juntai and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈榮祿大夫、陝西行省平章政事、柱國，追封涼國公，諡忠壯。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted grand master of glorious blessing, grand councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, pillar of the state, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him grand master of glorious blessing, Shaanxi grand councillor, pillar of the state, Duke of Liang, with the title Zhongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 陳君用，字子材，延平人。

translations.literal: Chen Junyong, style name Zicai, was a man of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Junyong, whose style name was Zicai, came from Yanping.

sentences.zh: 少負氣，勇猛過人。

translations.literal: In youth he bore spirit; his bravery surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was spirited and surpassingly brave.

sentences.zh: 紅巾起江淮，由撫、盱入閩，閩閫授君用南平縣尹，給錢五萬緡，俾募千兵，君用散家財繼之，導官軍復建陽、浦城等縣。

translations.literal: When the Red Turbans arose on the Huai and Yangzi, entering Min by Fu and Chu, the Min authorities appointed Junyong magistrate of Nanping County, gave fifty thousand strings of cash, and had him recruit a thousand troops; Junyong dispersed family wealth to continue this and guided government troops to recover Jianyang, Pucheng, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: When Red Turbans swept the Huai and Yangzi and entered Fujian, authorities made him magistrate of Nanping, gave him funds to raise a thousand men, spent his own fortune to match it, and helped recover Jianyang and Pucheng.

sentences.zh: 以功授同知建寧路事。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed associate administrator of Jianning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he was made associate administrator of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 亡何，賊圍福州，尹用率兵往援，大敗賊眾，廉訪僉事郭興祖，佩君用明珠虎符，使權同知副都元帥。

translations.literal: Before long bandits besieged Fuzhou; Junyong led troops to relieve it and greatly defeated the bandit multitude; surveillance vice commissioner Guo Xingzu hung on Junyong the pearl tiger tally and had him act as associate deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels besieged Fuzhou. He relieved the city with a great victory. Vice commissioner Guo Xingzu gave him the pearl tiger tally as acting associate deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵逾北嶺，至連江，阻水而陣。

translations.literal: He thereupon led troops over the northern ridge to Lianjiang and arrayed across the water.
translations.idiomatic: He marched over the northern ridge to Lianjiang and formed battle lines across the water.

sentences.zh: 君用曰：「今日不盡殺賊，吾不復生還矣。」

translations.literal: Junyong said: "Today if I do not utterly kill the bandits, I shall not return alive."
translations.idiomatic: Junyong said, "Unless I destroy every rebel today, I will not return alive."

sentences.zh: 乃率壯士六十人，徒涉斬殺。

translations.literal: He thereupon led sixty sturdy men, waded across and beheaded and killed.
translations.idiomatic: He waded the water with sixty men and cut them down.

sentences.zh: 賊稍潰，既而復合，君用大呼轉戰，中槍而死。

translations.literal: The bandits slightly broke; before long they combined again; Junyong shouted loudly and turned to battle; he was struck by a spear and died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels wavered, then rallied. Junyong fought on shouting until a spear killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈懷遠大將軍、浙東道宣慰司同知、副元帥、輕車都尉、潁川郡侯，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted general of far pacification, associate administrator of the Zhedong Pacification Commission, deputy commander, commander of light chariots, and Marquis of Yingchuan, with the posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him general of far pacification, Zhedong associate administrator, deputy commander, commander of light chariots, Marquis of Yingchuan, with the title Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 卜理牙敦，北庭人，累官至山南廉訪使，治中興。

translations.literal: Buli Yadun, a man of Beiting, rose through offices to surveillance commissioner of Shannan and governed Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Buli Yadun of Beiting rose to Shannan surveillance commissioner and governed Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 中興為江漢籓屏，卜理牙敦每按臨所部，威惠翕然。

translations.literal: Zhongxing was the screen of the Jiang and Han; whenever Buli Yadun inspected his jurisdiction, authority and kindness worked together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing guarded the Jiang-Han frontier; his tours united sternness and kindness.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，寇犯中興，卜理牙敦以兵與抗，射賊多死，賊稍退。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng bandits invaded Zhongxing; Buli Yadun resisted with troops, shooting bandits—many died—and the bandits slightly retreated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 rebels attacked Zhongxing. He fought back, killing many with his bow, and they briefly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日，复擁眾來襲東門，卜理牙敦力與之戰，被執，不屈而死。

translations.literal: The next day they again gathered crowds to assault the east gate; Buli Yadun strove in battle with them, was seized, and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they returned to assault the east gate. He fought until captured and died unyielding.

sentences.zh: 又明日，賊復來攻，前中興判官上都統兵出擊之。

translations.literal: Again the next day bandits came to attack; the former Zhongxing judge Shangdu led troops out to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The following day rebels attacked again. Former judge Shangdu led troops out.

sentences.zh: 既而東門失守，上都倉黃反斗，力屈，賊執之使降，上都大罵，賊怒，刳其腹、刲其肉而死。

translations.literal: Before long the east gate was lost; Shangdu in panic turned to fight; strength failed; bandits seized him and made him surrender; Shangdu cursed loudly; bandits in rage disemboweled him and sliced his flesh and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The east gate fell. Shangdu fought in confusion until captured. Ordered to submit, he cursed; they disemboweled him and cut his flesh from his body.

sentences.zh: 潮海，扎剌台氏，由國子生入官，為靖安縣達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Chaohai, of the Jalut clan, entered office from Imperial Academy student and became darughachi of Jing'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Chaohai of the Jalut clan entered through the Imperial Academy and became darughachi of Jing'an County.

sentences.zh: 至正十二年，蘄黃賊起，潮海與縣尹黃紹同集義兵，為御賊計。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhizheng Qi-Huang bandits arose; Chaohai together with magistrate Huang Shao gathered righteous troops to plan defense against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1352 Qi-Huang rebels rose. Chaohai and magistrate Huang Shao raised militia to defend the county.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊兵數万由武寧來寇，紹赴行省求援，潮海獨率眾與戰於像湖，大破之。

translations.literal: Before long tens of thousands of bandit troops came from Wuning to invade; Shao went to the branch secretariat to seek relief; Chaohai alone led the multitude to fight at Xiang Lake and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon tens of thousands came from Wuning. Shao sought aid at the secretariat while Chaohai alone routed them at Xiang Lake.

sentences.zh: 乃起進士胡鬥元、塗淵、舒慶遠、甘棠等謀畫，而以勇士黃雲為前鋒。

translations.literal: He then raised jinshi Hu Douyuan, Tu Yuan, Shu Qingyuan, Gan Tang, and others to plan, while making the brave warrior Huang Yun the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He enlisted jinshi Hu Douyuan, Tu Yuan, Shu Qingyuan, and Gan Tang to plan strategy, with warrior Huang Yun as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 自二月至於八月，戰屢捷，擒賊將洪元帥。

translations.literal: From the second month to the eighth they fought repeatedly with victory, capturing the bandit general Hong Yuanshuai.
translations.idiomatic: From the second to the eighth month they won repeatedly and captured rebel general Hong Yuanshuai.

sentences.zh: 而賊黨益盛，黃雲戰死，我軍挫衄，潮海遂被圍，尋為賊所執，殺於富州。

translations.literal: But the bandit party grew stronger; Huang Yun died in battle; our army was checked and broken; Chaohai was thereupon surrounded and shortly was seized by bandits and killed at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels grew stronger. Huang Yun fell; the army broke. Chaohai was surrounded, captured, and killed at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子民安圖，襲父職，為本縣達魯花赤。

translations.literal: His son Minantu inherited his father's post as darughachi of this county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Minantu inherited the darughachi post.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帥眾敗走賊將，复縣治。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he led troops to defeat and rout a bandit general and restored county administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353 he routed a rebel commander and restored order.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賊兵復至，民安圖迎戰，力竭，賊執而呙之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandit troops came again; Minantu went out to battle; strength was exhausted; bandits seized him and cut his throat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 rebels returned. Minantu fought until spent, was seized, and had his throat cut.

sentences.zh: 紹字仲先，臨川人。

translations.literal: Shao, style name Zhongxian, was a man of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shao, whose style name was Zhongxian, came from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 登至正八年進士第，以求援出靖安，而道阻絕，遇官軍，護紹得入龍興。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Zhizheng and went out to seek relief, but the road was cut off; he met government troops who escorted Shao into Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in 1348 and set out for aid, but roads were cut. Government troops escorted him to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 而龍興亦被圍，其後圍解，紹乃與民安圖招諭叛境，過建昌之高坪，遇賊，紹與戰不勝，正衣冠怒罵，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Longxing too was besieged; afterward the siege was lifted; Shao then together with Minantu summoned and instructed the rebel territory; passing Gaoping in Jianchang they met bandits; Shao fought but could not prevail, straightened his robes and cursed angrily, and was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Longxing was also besieged, then relieved. Shao and Minantu went to pacify rebel districts; at Gaoping in Jianchang he fought, failed, straightened his robes, cursed, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 鬥元字元浩，靖安人。

translations.literal: Douyuan, style name Yuanhao, was a man of Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Douyuan, whose style name was Yuanhao, came from Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 至正十年，領江西鄉薦第一，下第，署鰲溪書院山長。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhizheng he led first place in the Jiangxi provincial recommendation, failed the final examination, and was appointed head of Aoxi Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1350 he topped the Jiangxi provincial exams but failed the palace exam and became head of Aoxi Academy.

sentences.zh: 賊至靖安，掠鬥元鄉里，鬥元以鄉兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: When bandits reached Jing'an and plundered Douyuan's home district, Douyuan with township troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels raided his home district he beat them back with local militia.

sentences.zh: 入縣治，與潮海共圖戰守。

translations.literal: He entered the county seat and together with Chaohai planned battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Chaohai at the county seat to organize defense.

sentences.zh: 及潮海被執，賊脅之使降，鬥元罵不屈。

translations.literal: When Chaohai was seized, bandits coerced him to surrender; Douyuan cursed and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When Chaohai was captured rebels tried to make Douyuan submit; he cursed and refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以土埋其腰，不死，又縛置暗室。

translations.literal: They therefore buried him in earth up to his waist; he did not die; they again bound him and placed him in a dark room.
translations.idiomatic: They buried him to the waist but he lived. They bound him in a dark room.

sentences.zh: 鬥元僕牆以出，逃入深山，狂罵而死。

translations.literal: Douyuan broke through the wall and escaped, fled into deep mountains, and died madly cursing.
translations.idiomatic: He broke through the wall, fled to the mountains, and died still cursing.

sentences.zh: 黃雲，撫州人，寓靖安，素以勇捷稱，每接戰，獨以身當敵。

translations.literal: Huang Yun, a man of Fuzhou living in Jing'an, was by nature known for courage and agility; whenever he joined battle he alone took the enemy on his body.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yun of Fuzhou, living in Jing'an, was famed for courage; in every fight he faced the enemy alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗為數十人所圍，即奮身躍出。

translations.literal: Once he was surrounded by several tens of men and immediately exerted his body and leaped out.
translations.idiomatic: Once surrounded by dozens, he leaped clear of the ring.

sentences.zh: 至是，身中數十槍，噴血罵賊而死。

translations.literal: At this time his body received several tens of spear wounds; spurting blood he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Now pierced by dozens of spears, he spat blood, cursed the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 魏中立，字伯時，濟南人。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongli, style name Boshi, was a man of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongli, whose style name was Boshi, came from Jinan.

sentences.zh: 由國子伴讀歷官至陝西行台御史中丞，遷守饒州。

translations.literal: From Imperial Academy companion reader he rose through offices to investigating censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat and was transferred to defend Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Imperial Academy companion reader he became Shaanxi investigating censor, then defender of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 賊既陷湖廣，分攻州郡，官軍多疲懦不能拒，所在無賴子多乘間竊發，不旬日，眾輒數万，皆短衣草屢，齒木為杷，削竹為槍，截緋帛為巾襦，彌野皆赤。

translations.literal: After bandits had overrun Huguang they divided forces to attack prefectures and counties; government troops were mostly weary and cowardly and could not resist; wherever they were, worthless fellows often seized the interval to rise in secret, and within ten days the multitude would reach tens of thousands—all in short grass and straw sandals, teeth wood for hoes, bamboo cut for spears, red silk cut for jackets and trousers, filling the wilds all red.
translations.idiomatic: After Huguang fell, rebels attacked everywhere. Government troops were feeble. Ruffians rose in days to tens of thousands—barefoot in grass sandals, armed with wooden hoes and bamboo spears, dressed in red, the countryside turned crimson.

sentences.zh: 中立聞警，即率丁壯，分塞險要，戒守備。

translations.literal: Zhongli heard the alarm and immediately led sturdy youths, divided to block strategic points, and warned the garrison to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the alarm, he led stout youths to hold the passes and ordered the garrison to prepare.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊至，達魯花赤馬來出戰，不能發一矢，賊愈逼。

translations.literal: Shortly bandits arrived; the darughachi Malai went out to battle and could not shoot a single arrow; bandits pressed closer.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came. Darughachi Malai rode out but could not shoot an arrow as they closed in.

sentences.zh: 中立以義兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Zhongli with righteous troops struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongli's militia drove them back.

sentences.zh: 已而賊復合，遂為所執，以紅衣被其身，中立叱之，鬚髯盡張。

translations.literal: Before long bandits combined again and he was thereupon seized; they put a red garment on his body; Zhongli rebuked them and his beard and whiskers all bristled.
translations.idiomatic: They returned in force and seized him, dressing him in red. He rebuked them, beard bristling.

sentences.zh: 賊執歸蘄水，欲屈其從己。

translations.literal: The bandits took him back to Qishui and wished to bend him to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: They took him to Qishui and tried to win him over.

sentences.zh: 中立大罵不已，遂被害。

translations.literal: Zhongli cursed loudly without cease and thereupon met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed without cease until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊又犯信州，信州總管於大本以​​土兵備禦。

translations.literal: Before long bandits again invaded Xinzhou; Xinzhou intendant Yu Daben defended with local troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebels struck Xinzhou. Intendant Yu Daben defended with local troops.

sentences.zh: 賊首項甲破東門而入，執大本，至蘄​​水為俘獻。

translations.literal: Bandit chieftain Xiang Jia broke through the east gate and entered, seized Daben, and brought him to Qishui as a captive to present.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Xiang Jia broke the east gate, seized Daben, and sent him to Qishui as a prize.

sentences.zh: 偽主釋其縛，畀偽印一紐，且命以官。

translations.literal: The false lord released his bonds, gave him a false seal, and moreover ordered him to office.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader freed him, gave a false seal, and offered office.

sentences.zh: 大本投印於地，而指偽主痛詈之，遂亦遇害。

translations.literal: Daben threw the seal to the ground and pointed at the false lord, cursing him bitterly, and thereupon also met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Daben threw the seal down, pointed at the rebel chief, cursed him, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 大本字德中，密州人，始由儒學教諭入官云。

translations.literal: Daben, style name Dezhong, was a man of Mizhou; he first entered office from Confucian school instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Daben, whose style name was Dezhong, came from Mizhou and had entered service as a Confucian school instructor.
